'''Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo'''{{efn|{{bulleted list|English pronunciation: {{IPAc-en|ˈ|k|l|aʊ|d|i|ə|_|ˈ|ʃ|eɪ|n|b|ɔː|m}} {{respell|KLOW|dee|ə|_|SHAYN|bawm}}; {{IPA|es-419|ˈklawðja ˈʃejmbawm ˈpaɾðo|-|Csamex.ogg|small=no}}.<ref>{{cite web |title=Claudia: El Documental |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=E9LJanPjARc&t=19s |via=YouTube |date=20 December 2023 |publisher=Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo |access-date=4 June 2024 |archive-date=5 June 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240605025907/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=E9LJanPjARc&t=19s |url-status=live}}</ref>}}}} (born 24 June 1962) is a Mexican politician, [[energy]] and [[climate change]] scientist, and academic who has been serving as the 66th [[president of Mexico]] since 2024. She is the [[List of elected and appointed female heads of state and government|first woman]] and the first person of [[History of the Jews in Mexico|Jewish]]{{efn|[[Carlos Salinas de Gortari]], president of Mexico from 1988 to 1994, is of partial colonial-era Sephardic Jewish descent.<ref>{{cite web |title=Salinas de Gortari obtuvo nacionalidad española por origen judío sefaradí |url=https://www.enlacejudio.com/2022/10/30/salinas-de-gortari-obtuvo-nacionalidad-espanola-por-origen-judio-sefaradi/ |website=Enlace Judío |access-date=4 June 2024 |language=es-MX |date=30 October 2022 |archive-date=5 June 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240605025836/https://www.enlacejudio.com/2022/10/30/salinas-de-gortari-obtuvo-nacionalidad-espanola-por-origen-judio-sefaradi/ |url-status=live}}</ref>}} heritage to hold the office.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Madry |first1=Kylie |last2=Valentine |first2=Hilaire |date=2 June 2024 |title=Mexico's Sheinbaum poised to become first woman president |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/mexicans-vote-election-seen-crowning-first-female-president-2024-06-02/ |publisher=Reuters}}</ref><ref name="AP News-2024a">{{Cite web |date=22 April 2024 |title=Mexico's likely next president would be its first leader with a Jewish background |url=https://apnews.com/article/mexico-election-claudia-sheinbaum-judaism-catholicism-5932fcf5d74c215ae0e08a40eff8a64f |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240528191513/https://apnews.com/article/mexico-election-claudia-sheinbaum-judaism-catholicism-5932fcf5d74c215ae0e08a40eff8a64f |archive-date=28 May 2024 |access-date=3 June 2024 |publisher=AP News |language=en}}</ref><ref name="france24.com">{{Cite web |date=3 June 2024 |title=Ruling leftist party candidate Sheinbaum elected Mexico's first female president |url=https://www.france24.com/en/americas/20240603-sheinbaum-set-to-win-mexico-election-becoming-first-female-president |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240603063457/https://www.france24.com/en/americas/20240603-sheinbaum-set-to-win-mexico-election-becoming-first-female-president |archive-date=3 June 2024 |access-date=3 June 2024}}</ref><ref name=":9">{{Cite web |date=2024-06-03 |title=Mexico's first female president is also its first Jewish president |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/news/latino/claudia-sheinbaum-mexico-president-jewish-first-woman-rcna155179 |access-date=2026-05-22 |website=NBC News |language=en}}</ref> A member of the [[Morena (political party)|National Regeneration Movement]] (Morena), she previously served as [[List of mayors of Mexico City|Head of Government]] of [[Mexico City]] from 2018 to 2023. In 2025, ''[[Forbes]]'' ranked Sheinbaum as [[Forbes list of the World's 100 Most Powerful Women|the fifth most powerful woman in the world]].<ref>{{cite web |author=Roberta Maddalena |title=Giorgia Meloni è la terza donna più potente del mondo. Prima Ursula von der Leyen |trans-title="Giorgia Meloni is the third most powerful woman in the world. First is Ursula von der Leyen."|date=12 December 2024 |url=https://forbes.it/2024/12/12/100-donne-potenti-mondo-meloni-podio/ |language=IT}}</ref>

A [[scientist]] by profession, Sheinbaum received her doctorate in [[energy engineering]] from the [[National Autonomous University of Mexico]] (UNAM). She has co-authored over 100 articles and two books on energy, the environment, and [[sustainable development]]. She contributed to the [[Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change]] and, in 2018, was named one of [[100 Women (BBC)|BBC's ''100 Women'']].<ref>{{Cite news |date=19 November 2018 |title=BBC 100 Women 2018: Who is on the list? |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/world-46225037 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190107022254/https://www.bbc.com/news/world-46225037%20 |archive-date=7 January 2019 |access-date=23 July 2019 |publisher=BBC News |language=en-GB}}</ref> She was subsequently awarded the Sustainability Medal by the Nobel Sustainability Trust in 2024.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Nobel Sustainability Trust |first1= The |title=Medals of Outstanding Contribution to Sustainability 2024. |url=https://www.nobelsustainabilitytrust.org/the-sustainability-medal-2024|website=NST |date=18 October 2024 |access-date=4 January 2026}}</ref>

Sheinbaum joined the [[Party of the Democratic Revolution]] (PRD) in 1989. From 2000 to 2006, she served as secretary of the environment in the Federal District under [[Andrés Manuel López Obrador]]. She left the PRD in 2014 to join López Obrador's splinter movement, Morena, and was elected mayor of [[Tlalpan]] borough in 2015. In [[2018 Mexican general election#Mexico City|2018]], she became Head of Government of Mexico City, focusing on security, public transport, and social programs, while also overseeing major crises such as the [[COVID-19 pandemic]] and the [[Mexico City Metro overpass collapse]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Muñoz-Ledo |first=Rocío |date=3 June 2024 |title=ANÁLISIS: Así fue la gestión de Claudia Sheinbaum como jefa de Gobierno de la Ciudad de México |trans-title="ANALYSIS: This is how Claudia Sheinbaum managed her term as Head of Government of Mexico City"|url=https://cnnespanol.cnn.com/2024/06/03/analisis-asi-fue-gestion-claudia-sheinbaum-jefa-gobierno-ciudad-mexico-orix |access-date=20 April 2025 |website=CNN |language=es}}</ref><ref name="VOA-2018">{{Cite web |date=5 December 2018 |title=Mexico City's 1st Elected Female Mayor Takes Office |url=https://www.voanews.com/a/mexico-city-first-elected-female-mayor-claudia-sheinbaum-takes-office/4688400.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230907031828/https://www.voanews.com/a/mexico-city-first-elected-female-mayor-claudia-sheinbaum-takes-office/4688400.html |archive-date=7 September 2023 |access-date=7 September 2023 |publisher=VOA |language=en}}</ref> She resigned in 2023 to run for president and won Morena's nomination over [[Marcelo Ebrard]].<ref name="ABC News-2023">{{Cite web |date=6 September 2023 |title=Former Mexico City Mayor Claudia Sheinbaum to be the ruling party's presidential candidate |url=https://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory/former-mexico-city-mayor-claudia-sheinbaum-ruling-partys-102985068 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230907030244/https://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory/former-mexico-city-mayor-claudia-sheinbaum-ruling-partys-102985068 |archive-date=7 September 2023 |access-date=7 September 2023 |publisher=ABC News |language=en}}</ref> In the [[2024 Mexican general election|2024 presidential election]], she defeated [[Xóchitl Gálvez]] in a landslide.<ref>{{Cite web |date=3 June 2024 |title=Mexico elects Sheinbaum as first woman president |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cp4475gwny1o |access-date=20 April 2025 |website=www.bbc.com |language=en-GB}}</ref>

As president, Sheinbaum enacted a series of [[Constitutional amendment|constitutional reform]]s with the support of her legislative supermajority, including enshrining social programs into the [[Constitution of Mexico|Constitution]], reversing key aspects of the 2013 energy reform to strengthen state control over the energy sector, mandating that the minimum wage increase be above the rate of inflation, and introducing universal healthcare.

== Early life and family ==
Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo was born on 24 June 1962 in [[Mexico City]], within a [[Mexican Jews|Mexican Jewish]] religiously unobservant family.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.timesofisrael.com/mexico-city-elects-first-ever-jewish-mayor-exit-poll-shows/|title=Mexico City elects first-ever Jewish mayor, exit poll shows|access-date=27 March 2024|author=AFP|date=2 July 2018|website=The Times of Israel|language=en}}</ref><ref name=":9" /><ref>{{Cite news|title=Claudia Sheinbaum is the first Jewish person to reach the presidency in Mexico|url=https://www.nytimes.com/es/2024/06/03/espanol/claudia-sheinbaum-judia-presidente-mexico.html|newspaper=The New York Times|date=3 June 2024|access-date=4 June 2024|issn=0362-4331|language=es|first=Simón|last=Romero}}</ref> She is the second child of chemist [[Carlos Sheinbaum Yoselevitz]] and biologist [[Annie Pardo Cemo]].<ref name="La Razon">{{cite web |url=https://www.razon.com.mx/me-separe-de-carlos-imaz-de-comun-acuerdo-hace-un-ano/ |title="I separated from Carlos Ímaz by mutual agreement a year ago" |access-date=4 January 2018 |last=Belsasso |first=Bibiana |date=8 May 2017 |newspaper=[[La Razón de México]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180105233646/https://www.razon.com.mx/me-separe-de-carlos-imaz-de-comun-acuerdo-hace-un-ano/ |archive-date=5 January 2018}}</ref><ref name="SCMP">{{Cite news|title=Claudia Sheinbaum is first woman elected Mexico City mayor|url=https://www.scmp.com/news/world/americas/article/2153357/claudia-sheinbaum-first-woman-elected-mexico-city-mayor-defying|access-date=7 July 2018|newspaper=South China Morning Post|language=en}}</ref>

Carlos Sheinbaum was of [[Ashkenazi Jews|Ashkenazi Jewish]] descent. His father, Chone Juan Sheinbaum Abramovitz,<ref name="SonoraPresente">{{cite web |title=La singular y discreta historia familiar de Claudia Sheinbaum |url=https://sonorapresente.com/2024/06/la-singular-y-discreta-historia-familiar-de-claudia-sheinbaum/ |website=SonoraPresente |access-date=16 February 2025 |language=es |date=4 June 2024}}</ref> had emigrated from [[Lithuania]] in 1928, becoming a jewelry merchant and a member of the [[Mexican Communist Party]]. Annie Pardo is from a [[Sephardi Jewish]] family who arrived in Mexico in 1946, after fleeing from the [[The Holocaust in Bulgaria|persecution of Jews in Bulgaria during World War II]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=Silverstein |first=Andrew |url=https://forward.com/news/622618/mexico-president-claudia-sheinbaum-jewish-family-holocaust|title=Exclusive: Mexico's new Jewish president has not been telling the truth about her family's Holocaust story|access-date=20 April 2025|date=14 June 2024|publisher=Forward}}</ref> Pardo became the first Sephardic woman to be an academic at the [[Instituto Politécnico Nacional]].<ref name="SonoraPresente"/><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.enlacejudio.com/2018/12/17/judios-y-cientificos-la-familia-de-claudia-sheinbaum/|title=Jews and scientists. The family of Claudia Sheinbaum|access-date=27 March 2024|author=Enlace Judío México|date=18 December 2018|website=Enlace Judío|language=es-MX}}</ref>

Sheinbaum's parents were actively involved in Mexican [[Left-wing politics|left-wing]] circles during the 1960s, participating in protests, workers' movements, and student uprisings.<ref>{{Cite news|title=She was an example of life: Annie Pardo Semo|url=https://www.jornada.com.mx/2014/09/28/politica/003n3pol|date=28 September 2024|access-date=22 March 2023|newspaper=La Jornada}}</ref>

Sheinbaum has two siblings. Her older brother, Julio, is a [[physicist]]<ref name="sciencemag1">{{cite web |last=Wade |first=Lizzie |url=https://www.science.org/content/article/can-environmental-engineer-poised-become-mayor-fix-mexico-city |title=Can this environmental engineer—now elected mayor—fix Mexico City? |work=[[Science Magazine]] |publisher=[[American Association for the Advancement of Science|AAAS]] |date=2 July 2018 |access-date=25 April 2020 |archive-date=7 December 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211207170613/https://www.science.org/content/article/can-environmental-engineer-poised-become-mayor-fix-mexico-city |url-status=live}}</ref> and [[physical oceanography]] researcher at [[Ensenada Center for Scientific Research and Higher Education|CICESE]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Centro de Investigación Científica y de Educación Superior de Ensenada, Baja California |url=https://www.cicese.edu.mx/investigacion/personal_academico/871 |website=CICESE |publisher=CONAHCYT |access-date=15 June 2024 |archive-date=3 June 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240603211842/https://www.cicese.edu.mx/investigacion/personal_academico/871 |url-status=live}}</ref> Her younger sister, Adriana, is a teacher<ref>{{cite web |title=Educators |url=https://childrenslearninglab.com/educators/ |website=Children’s Learning Lab |access-date=15 June 2024 |archive-date=16 June 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240616060231/https://childrenslearninglab.com/educators/ |url-status=live}}</ref> who lives in the United States and is married to film director [[Rodrigo García (director)|Rodrigo García Barcha]], a son of Colombian writer and Nobel laureate [[Gabriel García Márquez]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kandell |first=Jonathan |date=17 April 2014 |title=Gabriel García Márquez, Conjurer of Literary Magic, Dies at 87 |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2014/04/18/books/gabriel-garcia-marquez-literary-pioneer-dies-at-87.html |website=[[The New York Times]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Miranda |first=Carolina |date=7 July 2021 |title=Rodrigo Garcia's memoir wrestles with the death of his father, novelist Gabriel García Márquez |url=https://www.latimes.com/entertainment-arts/books/story/2021-07-07/rodrigo-garcia-farewell-to-gabo-and-mercedes |website=[[Los Angeles Times]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Zamarripa |first1=Raymundo |title=¿Quiénes son los hermanos de los candidatos a la presidencia? |url=https://www.quien.com/politica/2024/03/19/quienes-son-los-hermanos-de-los-candidatos-a-la-presidencia |website=Quién |access-date=15 June 2024 |language=es |date=20 March 2024 |archive-date=16 June 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240616060302/https://www.quien.com/politica/2024/03/19/quienes-son-los-hermanos-de-los-candidatos-a-la-presidencia |url-status=live}}</ref>

== Academic career ==
Sheinbaum earned a bachelor's degree in [[physics]] at [[UNAM]] in 1989, a master's degree in 1994, and a [[Ph.D.]] in [[energy engineering]] in 1995.<ref name="themazatlanpost1">{{cite news |date=2 July 2018 |title=Mexico City chooses for the first time in history a Jew and female mayor, the scientist Claudia Sheinbaum |url=https://themazatlanpost.com/2018/07/02/mexico-city-chooses-for-the-first-time-in-history-a-jew-and-female-mayor-the-scientist-claudia-sheinbaum/ |access-date=25 April 2020 |newspaper=The Mazatlán Post |archive-date=28 July 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200728154855/https://themazatlanpost.com/2018/07/02/mexico-city-chooses-for-the-first-time-in-history-a-jew-and-female-mayor-the-scientist-claudia-sheinbaum/ |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="sciencemag1"/><ref name="Times of Israel-2018">{{Cite news |url=https://www.timesofisrael.com/mexico-city-elects-first-ever-jewish-mayor-exit-poll-shows/ |title=Mexico City elects first-ever Jewish mayor, exit poll shows |date=2 July 2018 |publisher=The Times of Israel |access-date=3 July 2018 |archive-date=5 October 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201005163254/https://www.timesofisrael.com/mexico-city-elects-first-ever-jewish-mayor-exit-poll-shows/ |url-status=live}}</ref>

Sheinbaum completed the work for her Ph.D. thesis between 1991 and 1994 at the [[Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory]] in [[California]]. While working for the laboratory, she analyzed energy use in the [[Transportation in Mexico|Mexican transportation sector]] and published studies on the trends in Mexican building energy use.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Mexico City Mayor-Elect Claudia Sheinbaum Visits Berkeley Lab |url=https://international.lbl.gov/news/mexico-city-mayor-elect-claudia |access-date=8 December 2023 |website=international.lbl.gov |archive-date=3 June 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240603050146/https://international.lbl.gov/news/mexico-city-mayor-elect-claudia |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="jpost1">{{cite web |last=Weber |first=Jonathan |url=https://www.jpost.com/diaspora/mexico-city-elects-first-jewish-female-mayor-561329 |title=Mexico City elects first Jewish, female mayor |work=The Jerusalem Post |date=2 July 2018 |access-date=25 April 2020 |archive-date=30 December 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201230174148/https://www.jpost.com/diaspora/mexico-city-elects-first-jewish-female-mayor-561329 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="dailycal1">{{Cite web |date=6 July 2018 |title=Former Berkeley Lab researcher elected as Mexico City mayor |url=https://dailycal.org/2018/07/06/former-berkeley-lab-researcher-elected-mexico-city-mayor/ |access-date=8 December 2023 |publisher=The Daily Californian |language=en |archive-date=18 December 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231218160032/https://dailycal.org/2018/07/06/former-berkeley-lab-researcher-elected-mexico-city-mayor |url-status=live}}</ref>

In 1995, Sheinbaum joined the faculty of the [[Engineering Institute|Institute of Engineering]] at UNAM.<ref name="sciencemag1"/> In 1999, she received the prize for being the best UNAM young researcher in engineering and technological innovation.<ref name="google1">{{cite book |title=Green CITYnomics: The Urban War against Climate Change |publisher=Routledge |author=Kenny Tang |date=2009 |isbn=9781351279420}}</ref>

In 2006, Sheinbaum returned to [[UNAM]] after a period in government and began publishing articles in scientific journals.<ref name="sciencemag1"/>

In 2007, Sheinbaum contributed to the "Industry" chapter of the {{abbr|WG3|Working Group III}} (Mitigation) section in the [[IPCC Fourth Assessment Report|Fourth Assessment Report]] of the [[Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change]] (IPCC)<ref>{{cite report|chapter=Chapter 7: Industry|pages=447–496|title=Climate Change 2007 – Mitigation of Climate Change: Working Group III"|publisher=IPCC|editor-last1=Mertz|editor-first1=B.|editor-last2=Davidson|editor-first2=O.|editor-last3=Bosch|editor-first3=P.|editor-last4=Dave|editor-first4=R.|editor-last5=Meyer|editor-first5=L.|access-date=19 December 2025|url=https://www.ipcc.ch/report/ar4/wg3/|year=2007}}</ref> and, in 2013, served as a lead author for the chapter in the [[IPCC Fifth Assessment Report]].<ref>"[https://www.ipcc.ch/site/assets/uploads/2018/02/ipcc_wg3_ar5_chapter10.pdf Industry Chapter10 IPCC Retrieved 2 July 2018] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180614040639/http://www.ipcc.ch/pdf/assessment-report/ar5/wg3/ipcc_wg3_ar5_chapter10.pdf |date=14 June 2018}}</ref>

== Early political career ==

During her time as a student at UNAM, Sheinbaum was a member of the University Student Council ({{lang|es|Consejo Estudiantil Universitario}}),<ref name="Belsasso-2017">{{Cite news|url=https://www.razon.com.mx/me-separe-de-carlos-imaz-de-comun-acuerdo-hace-un-ano/|title=Me separé de Carlos Ímaz de común acuerdo hace un año|last=Belsasso|first=Bibiana|date=8 May 2017|newspaper=[[La Razón de Mexico]]|access-date=2 July 2018|language=es|trans-title=I split with Carlos Ímaz by mutual agreement one year ago|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180105233646/https://www.razon.com.mx/me-separe-de-carlos-imaz-de-comun-acuerdo-hace-un-ano/|archive-date=5 January 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref> a group of students that would become the founding youth movement of the [[Party of the Democratic Revolution]] (PRD).<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.excelsior.com.mx/nacional/2016/09/12/1116346?phdjmgdjekngdjek|title=CEU: semillero de políticos; el movimiento estudiantil del 86|last=Robles de la Rosa|first=Leticia|date=12 September 2016|work=Excelsior|access-date=2 July 2018|language=es|trans-title=CEU: A hotbed of politicians; the student movement of '86|archive-date=31 July 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200731204155/https://www.excelsior.com.mx/nacional/2016/09/12/1116346?phdjmgdjekngdjek|url-status=live}}</ref>

[[File:Madrid y Ciudad de México, dispuestas a reforzar su mutua colaboración 01.jpg|thumb|Madrid mayor [[Manuela Carmena]] meets with Sheinbaum at the [[Cibeles Palace]]]]

Sheinbaum served as the secretary of the environment of the [[Federal District (Mexico)|Federal District]] from 5 December 2000 to 15 May 2006, appointed by [[Head of Government of the Federal District]] [[Andrés Manuel López Obrador]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Flores |first=José Luis |date=21 November 2000 |title=Presenta AMLO su gabinete |trans-title=AMLO presents his cabinet |url=http://archivo.eluniversal.com.mx/ciudad/19545.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200919111302/https://archivo.eluniversal.com.mx/ciudad/19545.html |archive-date=19 September 2020 |access-date=2 July 2018 |work=El Universal |language=es}}</ref> During her term, she was responsible for constructing an electronic vehicle registration center for Mexico City.<ref name="google1" /><ref>{{Cite news|url=http://archivo.eluniversal.com.mx/ciudad/21410.html|title=Crearán central de verificentros|last=Cardoso|first=Laura|date=27 December 2000|work=El Universal|access-date=2 July 2018|language=es|trans-title=Center of vehicular registration to be created|archive-date=19 September 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200919133904/https://archivo.eluniversal.com.mx/ciudad/21410.html|url-status=live}}</ref> She also oversaw the introduction of the [[Mexico City Metrobús|Metrobús]], a [[bus rapid transit]] system with dedicated lanes, and the construction of the second storey of Mexico City's [[ring road]], [[Anillo Periférico]].<ref name="sciencemag1"/>

Following López Obrador’s narrow loss in the [[2006 Mexican general election#Results|2006 presidential election]], Sheinbaum was tasked with assembling a team to investigate what he described as electoral fraud.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Rubí |first=Ricardo |date=5 December 2023 |title=Claudia Sheinbaum explica cómo analizó el "fraude electoral" de 2006 |url=https://heraldodemexico.com.mx/edicion-impresa/2023/12/5/claudia-sheinbaum-explica-como-analizo-el-fraude-electoral-de-2006-560216.html |access-date=11 May 2025 |website=El Heraldo de Mexico |language=spanish}}</ref> The group analyzed tally sheets and used data from the Preliminary Electoral Results Program (PREP), concluding that the main irregularity was the alleged alteration of vote totals on polling station records.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Aviles |first=Jaime |date=17 August 2006 |title=Video muestra violaciones en siete distritos electorales |url=https://www.jornada.com.mx/2006/08/17/index.php?section=politica&article=003n1pol |access-date=11 May 2025 |website=La Jornada}}</ref> Sheinbaum also presented video evidence of alleged violations, including tampered ballot packages and improperly sealed envelopes, in several districts.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /> The findings were submitted to the [[Electoral Tribunal of the Federal Judiciary]] (TEPJF) as part of a request for a full recount,<ref name=":0" /> which the tribunal ultimately denied.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Urrutia |first=Alonso |date=7 September 2006 |title=En breve acto, Calderón recibe constancia de presidente electo – La Jornada |url=https://www.jornada.com.mx/2006/09/07/index.php?section=politica&article=003n1pol |access-date=11 May 2025 |website=La Jornada}}</ref>

López Obrador included Sheinbaum in his proposed cabinet for the [[Secretariat of Environment and Natural Resources]] as part of his campaign for the [[2012 Mexican general election|2012 presidential election]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.lopezobrador.org.mx/gabinete2012/index.html|title=Propuesta de Gabinete de Andrés Manuel López Obrador |date=31 January 2012|website=Sitio Oficial de Andrés Manuel López Obrador|language=es|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120131213325/http://www.lopezobrador.org.mx/gabinete2012/index.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=31 January 2012|access-date=2 July 2018}}</ref> In 2014, she joined López Obrador's splinter movement, the [[National Regeneration Movement]] (Morena), which broke away from the mainstream left-wing party, the Party of the Democratic Revolution.<ref name="jpost1"/>

===Mayor of Tlalpan===
In the 2015 Federal District local elections, Sheinbaum was nominated by the National Regeneration Movement (Morena) for the mayorship of [[Tlalpan]].<ref>{{cite web |date=9 September 2018 |title=Claudia Sheinbaum |url=https://www.jpost.com/50-most-influential-jews/17-Claudia-Sheinbaum-565406 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191213083403/https://www.jpost.com/50-most-influential-jews/17-Claudia-Sheinbaum-565406 |archive-date=13 December 2019 |access-date=13 December 2019 |work=The Jerusalem Post}}</ref> She campaigned on a platform focused on improving public services and public spaces, reducing corruption, and implementing social programs for women and young adults.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2 June 2015 |title=La Jornada: Gobierno con el apoyo de los ciudadanos, ofrece Sheinbaum |url=https://www.jornada.com.mx/2015/06/02/capital/034n1cap |access-date=3 February 2025 |website=www.jornada.com.mx |language=es}}</ref> She won with 29.48% of the vote, flipping the borough from the Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD), which had governed the borough since 2000.

On 29 April 2016, city staff were ordered to demolish a wall that had been built illegally adjacent to a chapel ({{lang|es|Capilla del Señor de los Trabajos}}) in Tlalpan's Cultura Maya neighborhood.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Martínez Chacón |first1=Marcos |title=Gobierno de capital mexicana no promueve demolición de iglesias |url=https://apnews.com/article/ap-verifica-093291152983 |access-date=1 June 2024 |work=Associated Press News |date=18 August 2022 |archive-date=30 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231130092734/https://apnews.com/article/ap-verifica-093291152983 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.milenio.com/estados/desaloja-y-tira-capilla-la-delegacion-tlalpan |title=Desaloja y tira capilla la delegación Tlalpan |newspaper=Milenio Diario |language=es |date=30 April 2016 |access-date=28 December 2021 |archive-date=28 December 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211228214649/https://www.milenio.com/estados/desaloja-y-tira-capilla-la-delegacion-tlalpan |url-status=live}}</ref> The workers instructed to demolish the wall also destroyed part of the chapel's structure, including its sheet metal roof, and removed religious images.<ref name="Univ=chapel">{{cite web|url=https://www.eluniversal.com.mx/articulo/metropoli/cdmx/2016/05/4/recula-sheinbaum-levantara-capilla-que-ordeno-derribar|title=Recula Sheinbaum por capilla|newspaper=El Universal|language=es|date=4 May 2016|access-date=28 December 2021|archive-date=28 December 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211228214639/https://www.eluniversal.com.mx/articulo/metropoli/cdmx/2016/05/4/recula-sheinbaum-levantara-capilla-que-ordeno-derribar|url-status=live}}</ref> Juan Guillermo Blandón Pérez, the parish priest, alleged that Sheinbaum was responsible for demolishing the chapel and claimed that it was carried out without prior notification.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.razon.com.mx/ciudad/sheinbaum-tumba-capilla-y-tira-a-la-calle-crucifijos-imagenes/|title=Sheinbaum tumba capilla y tira a la calle crucifijos, imágenes...|newspaper=La Razón|language=es|date=2 May 2016|access-date=28 December 2021|archive-date=28 December 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211228214643/https://www.razon.com.mx/ciudad/sheinbaum-tumba-capilla-y-tira-a-la-calle-crucifijos-imagenes/|url-status=live}}</ref> Days after the chapel's demolition, borough authorities acknowledged their error.<ref>{{cite news |title=Falso que Claudia Sheinbaum planeara "acabar" con las iglesias en Tlalpan |url=https://animalpolitico.com/verificacion-de-hechos/desinformacion/falso-sheinbaum-acabar-iglesias-tlalpan?s=08 |access-date=1 June 2024 |work=Animal Político |date=25 September 2023 |archive-date=3 June 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240603061250/https://animalpolitico.com/verificacion-de-hechos/desinformacion/falso-sheinbaum-acabar-iglesias-tlalpan?s=08 |url-status=live}}</ref> Sheinbaum met with church representatives and proposed dividing the property in half to build a new chapel and a community art center.<ref name="Univ=chapel" />[[File:Colegio Enrique Rébsamen 01.jpg|thumb|Earthquake damage to the Enrique Rébsamen School]]
The Colegio Enrique Rébsamen, a private school in Tlalpan, collapsed during the [[2017 Puebla earthquake]], killing 19 children and seven adults. In September 2016, the city's Institute for Administrative Verification had ruled that the school's building infringed zoning regulations and was built higher than was allowed and that the owner, Mónica García Villegas, had presented falsified documents.<ref name="invea"/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://heraldodemexico.com.mx/nacional/2020/8/12/quien-es-miss-monica-maestra-que-enfrenta-un-juicio-por-el-caso-rebsamen-199560.html|title=¿Quién es Miss Mónica, maestra que enfrenta un juicio por el Caso Rébsamen?|newspaper=El Heraldo de México|date=12 August 2020|access-date=28 December 2021|archive-date=28 December 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211228214641/https://heraldodemexico.com.mx/nacional/2020/8/12/quien-es-miss-monica-maestra-que-enfrenta-un-juicio-por-el-caso-rebsamen-199560.html|url-status=live}}</ref> Sheinbaum faced criticism for not providing a complete account of the permits for the school's land use, construction, and operation.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://ruizhealytimes.com/sin-categoria/cinismo-y-cobardia-de-claudia-sheinbaum-en-la-tragedia-del-colegio-rebsamen/|title=Cinismo y cobardía de Claudia Sheinbaum en la tragedia del Colegio Rébsamen|newspaper=Ruiz-Healy Times|date=14 June 2018|access-date=28 December 2021|archive-date=28 December 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211228214640/https://ruizhealytimes.com/sin-categoria/cinismo-y-cobardia-de-claudia-sheinbaum-en-la-tragedia-del-colegio-rebsamen/|url-status=live}}</ref> Enrique Fuentes, a lawyer representing the deceased children's parents, stated that the mayor had an obligation to take action but had failed to do so, allowing the school to continue operating.<ref name="invea">{{cite web|url=https://www.eluniversal.com.mx/columna/hector-de-mauleon/nacion/claudia-sheinbaum-y-el-colegio-rebsamen|title=Claudia Sheinbaum y el Colegio Rébsamen|author=Héctor De Mauleón|author-link=Héctor de Mauleón|newspaper=El Universal|date=12 February 2018|access-date=28 December 2021|archive-date=28 December 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211228214638/https://www.eluniversal.com.mx/columna/hector-de-mauleon/nacion/claudia-sheinbaum-y-el-colegio-rebsamen|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 5 December 2017, Sheinbaum resigned to run for [[Head of Government of Mexico City]] as a candidate for the {{lang|es|[[Juntos Haremos Historia]]}} coalition ({{Literal translation|Together We Will Make History}}), composed of Morena, the [[Labor Party (Mexico)|Labor Party]] (PT), and the [[Social Encounter Party]] (PES).<ref>{{cite web |title=Claudia Sheinbaum, la científica que gobernará CDMX |url=https://politico.mx//central-electoral/elecciones-2018/cdmx/claudia-sheinbaum-la-cient%C3%ADfica-que-gobernar%C3%A1-cdmx/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200717012641/https://politico.mx/central-electoral/elecciones-2018/cdmx/claudia-sheinbaum-la-cient%C3%ADfica-que-gobernar%C3%A1-cdmx/ |archive-date=17 July 2020 |access-date=13 December 2019 |publisher=politico.mx}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Tello |first=Natividad |date=29 March 2018 |title=Estos son los candidatos de coalición 'Juntos Haremos Historia' en CDMX |trans-title=These are the candidates of the coalition "Together We Will Make History" in Mexico City |url=http://www.excelsior.com.mx/comunidad/estos-son-los-candidatos-de-coalicion-juntos-haremos-historia-en-cdmx/1229306 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200919072524/https://www.excelsior.com.mx/comunidad/estos-son-los-candidatos-de-coalicion-juntos-haremos-historia-en-cdmx/1229306 |archive-date=19 September 2020 |access-date=2 July 2018 |work=Excelsior |language=es}}</ref>

== 2018 campaign for the Head of Government of Mexico City ==
[[File:Resultado Elecciones CDMX por Demarcación Territorial.svg|thumb|Election results by borough in the [[2018 Mexican general election#Mexico City|2018 election for the Head of Government of Mexico City]]]]
In August 2017, Sheinbaum participated in a poll by the National Regeneration Movement to determine the party's [[candidate]] for the head of government of Mexico City.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Suárez |first=Gerardo |date=13 August 2017 |title=Candidato de Morena para 2018, por encuesta |trans-title=2018 Morena's candidate, by survey |url=https://www.eluniversal.com.mx/articulo/metropoli/cdmx/2017/08/13/candidato-de-morena-para-2018-por-encuesta/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240601212038/https://www.eluniversal.com.mx/articulo/metropoli/cdmx/2017/08/13/candidato-de-morena-para-2018-por-encuesta/ |archive-date=1 June 2024 |access-date=22 October 2024 |website=El Universal |language=es}}</ref> The other contenders were [[Martí Batres]], [[Mario Delgado (politician)|Mario Delgado]], and [[Ricardo Monreal]]. Sheinbaum secured first place with 15.9% of the vote, beating her closest opponent, Batres, by 5.8 points.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rueda |first=Rivelino |date=29 August 2017 |title=Monreal quedó en tercero, según la encuesta de Morena en la CDMX |trans-title=Monreal in third place, according to Morena's survey in Mexico City |url=https://www.elfinanciero.com.mx/nacional/morena-revela-metodologia-de-encuesta-de-cdmx/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240601212037/https://www.elfinanciero.com.mx/nacional/morena-revela-metodologia-de-encuesta-de-cdmx/ |archive-date=1 June 2024 |access-date=1 June 2024 |website=El Financiero |language=es}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=García |first=Jacobo |date=25 August 2017 |title=Sheinbaum, candidata del partido de López Obrador a la Ciudad de México |url=https://elpais.com/internacional/2017/08/25/mexico/1503624178_341550.html |access-date=7 September 2023 |work=El País |language=es |issn=1134-6582 |archive-date=7 September 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230907031828/https://elpais.com/internacional/2017/08/25/mexico/1503624178_341550.html |url-status=live}}</ref> On 5 December 2017, Sheinbaum stepped down as mayor of Tlalpan to register her pre-candidacy.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Corona |first1=Salvador |title=Sheinbaum deja Tlalpan; no acude a comparecer |url=https://www.eleconomista.com.mx/politica/Sheinbaum-deja-Tlalpan-no-acude-a-comparecer-20171205-0180.html |access-date=3 June 2024 |work=El Economista |date=6 December 2017 |archive-date=17 February 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180217181730/https://www.eleconomista.com.mx/politica/Sheinbaum-deja-Tlalpan-no-acude-a-comparecer-20171205-0180.html |url-status=live}}</ref>

At her campaign launch on 1 April 2018, Sheinbaum prioritized fighting crime, stating that she would hold regular public hearings, publish reported crime statistics, and rely on the Security Council for guidance. She committed to generating 1 million jobs during her term, maintaining the universal pension for seniors, and expanding the Mexico City Metrobús system to connect the city's outskirts with the center.<ref name="VOA-2018" /><ref>{{Cite web |date=1 April 2018 |title=En su arranque de campaña, Sheinbaum 'estrena' propuestas y equipo |url=https://politica.expansion.mx/cdmx/2018/04/01/en-su-arranque-de-campana-sheinbaum-estrena-propuestas-y-equipo |access-date=1 June 2024 |website=ADNPolítico |language=es |archive-date=3 June 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240603061354/https://politica.expansion.mx/cdmx/2018/04/01/en-su-arranque-de-campana-sheinbaum-estrena-propuestas-y-equipo |url-status=live}}</ref>

During the campaign period, Sheinbaum was accused by members of {{lang|es|[[Por México al Frente]]}} of being culpable for the collapse of the Colegio Enrique Rébsamen, a private school in Tlalpan, during the 2017 Puebla earthquake.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Acusan a Sheinbaum por caso Rébsamen |url=https://www.eluniversal.com.mx/metropoli/cdmx/acusan-sheinbaum-por-caso-rebsamen/ |access-date=1 June 2024 |website=El Universal |language=es |archive-date=1 June 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240601212041/https://www.eluniversal.com.mx/metropoli/cdmx/acusan-sheinbaum-por-caso-rebsamen/ |url-status=live}}</ref>

On 1 July 2018, Sheinbaum was elected to a six-year term as the head of government of Mexico City with 47.08% of the vote, defeating six other candidates.<ref>{{cite news |title=Claudia Sheinbaum aventaja conteo rápido con 47.08% de los votos |url=https://www.publimetro.com.mx/mx/noticias/2018/07/02/claudia-sheinbaum-aventaja-conteo-rapido-47-08-los-votos.html |access-date=3 June 2024 |work=Publímetro |date=2 July 2018 |archive-date=22 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230622214338/https://www.publimetro.com.mx/mx/noticias/2018/07/02/claudia-sheinbaum-aventaja-conteo-rapido-47-08-los-votos.html |url-status=live}}</ref>

== Head of Government of Mexico City (2018–2023) ==
[[File:Toma_de_protesta_de_Claudia_Sheinbaum_3.jpg|thumb|right|After taking charge as head of government, Claudia Sheinbaum went to the [[Teatro de la Ciudad]] to present her cabinet.]]
[[File:Senderos Seguros Conferencia Matutina 02.jpg|thumb|right|Sheinbaum with President Andrés Manuel López Obrador in late 2019]]
On 5 December 2018, Sheinbaum was inaugurated as [[Mexico City Head of Government|Mexico City's head of government]]. She became the first elected female head of government and the first to come from a Jewish background.<ref name="AP News-2024a" /><ref name="SCMP" /><ref name="jpost1" />

Sheinbaum's administration was characterized by a strong relationship with the federal government and President López Obrador. However, she took distinct approaches to certain issues, such as managing the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], where her scientific background shaped the city's response to the crisis.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Muñoz-Ledo |first=Rocío |date=3 June 2024 |title=ANÁLISIS: Así fue la gestión de Claudia Sheinbaum como jefa de Gobierno de la Ciudad de México |url=https://cnnespanol.cnn.com/2024/06/03/analisis-asi-fue-gestion-claudia-sheinbaum-jefa-gobierno-ciudad-mexico-orix/ |access-date=8 July 2024 |website=CNN |language=es |archive-date=27 June 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240627230657/https://cnnespanol.cnn.com/2024/06/03/analisis-asi-fue-gestion-claudia-sheinbaum-jefa-gobierno-ciudad-mexico-orix/ |url-status=live}}</ref>

Sheinbaum resigned on 16 June 2023 to participate in the internal selection for the Morena-led coalition, {{lang|es|[[Juntos Hacemos Historia]]}}, ahead of the [[2024 Mexican general election|2024 presidential election]]. Sheinbaum recommended Batres as substitute head of government,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ayala Espinosa |first=Camila |date=14 June 2023 |title=Sheinbaum propone a Martí Batres como jefe de Gobierno de CDMX |url=https://www.eleconomista.com.mx/politica/Sheinbaum-propone-a-Marti-Batres-como-jefe-de-Gobierno-de-CDMX-20230614-0069.html |access-date=15 August 2024 |website=El Economista}}</ref> a choice later ratified by the [[Congress of Mexico City]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Zamarrón |first=Israel |date=16 June 2023 |title=Martí Batres es oficialmente el nuevo jefe de gobierno de la Ciudad de México |url=https://www.forbes.com.mx/marti-batres-es-oficialmente-el-nuevo-jefe-de-gobierno-de-la-ciudad-de-mexico/ |access-date=15 August 2024 |website=Forbes México |language=es-MX}}</ref>

=== Crime and policing ===
Sheinbaum implemented a security strategy based on four pillars: addressing the root causes of violence through education and community programs; enhancing the quality and quantity of the police force; strengthening intelligence and investigative capabilities; and improving coordination among law enforcement agencies.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ayala Espinosa |first=Camila |date=8 February 2022 |title=Sheinbaum presume avances en estrategia de seguridad en la CDMX |url=https://www.eleconomista.com.mx/estados/Sheinbaum-presume-avances-en-estrategia-de-seguridad-en-la-CDMX-20220207-0051.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220816034554/http://www.eleconomista.com.mx/estados/Sheinbaum-presume-avances-en-estrategia-de-seguridad-en-la-CDMX-20220207-0051.html |archive-date=16 August 2022 |access-date=2 June 2024 |website=El Economista}}</ref>

Her tenure saw several high-profile incidents, including the resignation and later indictment of her first security secretary, Jesús Orta, on federal corruption charges;<ref>{{Cite news |date=10 August 2020 |title=Sheinbaum acepta que Jesús Orta fue designado por decisión personal |url=https://politica.expansion.mx/cdmx/2020/08/10/sheinbaum-acepta-que-jesus-orta-fue-una-designado-por-una-decision-personal |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240621235249/https://politica.expansion.mx/cdmx/2020/08/10/sheinbaum-acepta-que-jesus-orta-fue-una-designado-por-una-decision-personal |archive-date=21 June 2024 |access-date=8 July 2024 |website=ADNPolítico |language=es}}</ref> the [[Attempted assassination of Omar García Harfuch|attempted assassination]] of her second security secretary, [[Omar García Harfuch]];<ref>{{Cite web |last=García |first=Jacobo |date=21 June 2021 |title=Omar García Harfuch, the Mexican police chief who survived being shot at 414 times |url=https://english.elpais.com/usa/2021-06-21/omar-garcia-harfuch-the-mexican-police-chief-who-survived-being-shot-at-414-times.html |access-date=1 May 2025 |website=EL PAÍS English |language=en}}</ref> the escape of three inmates linked to the [[Sinaloa Cartel]];<ref>{{Cite news |last=Mota |first=José I. |date=31 January 2020 |title=En camioneta y por la puerta principal: la fuga de tres narcos del cartel de Sinaloa en Ciudad de México |url=https://elpais.com/internacional/2020/01/30/actualidad/1580420695_958687.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240622013756/https://elpais.com/internacional/2020/01/30/actualidad/1580420695_958687.html |archive-date=22 June 2024 |access-date=8 July 2024 |work=El País |language=es |issn=1134-6582}}</ref> and the widely publicized [[Killing of Ingrid Escamilla|femicide of Ingrid Escamilla]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=La indignación en México por el brutal asesinato de Ingrid Escamilla y la difusión de las fotos de su cadáver |url=https://www.bbc.com/mundo/noticias-america-latina-51469528 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240610070033/https://www.bbc.com/mundo/noticias-america-latina-51469528 |archive-date=10 June 2024 |access-date=8 July 2024 |work=BBC News Mundo |language=es}}</ref> Between 2018 and 2022, Mexico City's homicide rate declined from 17.9 to 8.6 per 100,000 people, although the city recorded 5,078 homicides in the first 52 months of her term—more than under her three immediate predecessors.<ref>{{Cite web |date=21 July 2023 |title=Ebrard vs Sheinbaum: ¿con quién hubo menos homicidios en CDMX y cómo se miden? |url=https://animalpolitico.com/verificacion-de-hechos/te-explico/ebrard-sheinbaum-homicidios-cdmx |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231201061511/https://animalpolitico.com/verificacion-de-hechos/te-explico/ebrard-sheinbaum-homicidios-cdmx |archive-date=1 December 2023 |access-date=2 June 2024 |website=Animal Politico |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Defunciones registradas por homicidio por entidad federativa |url=https://www.inegi.org.mx/app/tabulados/interactivos/?pxq=Mortalidad_Mortalidad_08_8c2b9aa2-3aa6-4fdb-9c15-7172f2600ef2 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240601202009/https://www.inegi.org.mx/app/tabulados/interactivos/?pxq=Mortalidad_Mortalidad_08_8c2b9aa2-3aa6-4fdb-9c15-7172f2600ef2 |archive-date=1 June 2024 |access-date=1 June 2024 |publisher=INEGI}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Graham |first1=Thomas |date=21 November 2023 |title=Is Mexico City's plummeting murder rate too good to be true? |url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2023/nov/21/mexico-city-murder-rate-dropped-disappeared-number-rises |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240603061406/https://www.theguardian.com/world/2023/nov/21/mexico-city-murder-rate-dropped-disappeared-number-rises |archive-date=3 June 2024 |access-date=1 June 2024 |work=The Guardian}}</ref>

==== Gender violence ====
In 2019, Sheinbaum declared a gender violence alert in response to rising public concern. Her administration launched a citywide hotline and built over 700 kilometers of "safe corridors" to improve security for women in public spaces.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Navarrete |first=Shelma |date=21 November 2019 |title=Sheinbaum decreta Alerta de Violencia de Género en la CDMX |url=https://politica.expansion.mx/cdmx/2019/11/21/sheinbaum-decreta-alerta-de-violencia-de-genero-en-la-cdmx |access-date=13 August 2024 |website=ADNPolítico |language=es}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Cruz |first=Alejandro |date=24 November 2022 |title=Alerta de género redujo delitos contra mujeres en CDMX, dice Sheinbaum |url=https://www.jornada.com.mx/notas/2022/11/24/capital/alerta-de-genero-redujo-delitos-contra-mujeres-en-cdmx-dice-sheinbaum/ |access-date=13 August 2024 |website=La Jornada |language=es}}</ref>

==== Gun control ====
Sheinbaum promoted a voluntary gun buyback program, allowing residents to anonymously exchange firearms for cash. By the end of her term, the program had collected more than 6,500 weapons, including over 1,300 long guns, and had cost about MX$40 million.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Piden cultura de paz, en lugar de armas |url=https://www.eluniversal.com.mx/metropoli/piden-cultura-de-paz-en-lugar-de-armas/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240620034834/https://www.eluniversal.com.mx/metropoli/piden-cultura-de-paz-en-lugar-de-armas/ |archive-date=20 June 2024 |access-date=8 July 2024 |website=El Universal |language=es}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Con "Sí al desarme, sí a la paz" se han reducido homicidios y lesiones: Sheinbaum |url=https://www.proceso.com.mx/nacional/cdmx/2021/9/21/con-si-al-desarme-si-la-paz-se-han-reducido-homicidios-lesiones-sheinbaum-272404.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240625212254/https://www.proceso.com.mx/nacional/cdmx/2021/9/21/con-si-al-desarme-si-la-paz-se-han-reducido-homicidios-lesiones-sheinbaum-272404.html |archive-date=25 June 2024 |access-date=8 July 2024 |website=www.proceso.com.mx |language=spanish}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://extbox.ibero.mx/portaldocentes/url/20_1_33_95101_4.pdf|title=SÍ AL DESARME, SÍ A LA PAZ 2024 – GACETA CDMX 19/01/24|website=extbox.ibero.mx|language=es}}</ref>

==== Organized crime ====
Her government targeted criminal groups including the [[Jalisco New Generation Cartel]] and [[La Unión Tepito]], resulting in the arrest of multiple key figures. Analysts credited these operations to improved intelligence coordination led by Secretary of Security Omar García Harfuch.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Castellanos-Lanzarin |first=Hilda |date=11 April 2023 |title=CDMX suma 120 líderes generadores de violencia detenidos: García Harfuch |url=https://www.excelsior.com.mx/comunidad/cdmx-suma-120-lideres-generadores-de-violencia-detenidos-harfuch/1581076 |access-date=13 August 2024 |website=Excélsior |language=es-MX}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=9 September 2023 |title=Omar García Harfuch, artífice del modelo de inteligencia para combate a grupos crimínales |url=https://mvsnoticias.com/nacional/cdmx/2023/9/9/omar-garcia-harfuch-artifice-del-modelo-de-inteligencia-para-combate-grupos-criminales-606103.html |access-date=13 August 2024 |website=MVS Noticias |language=es}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Santiago |first=David |date=6 September 2023 |title=Harfuch, el aspirante de CDMX que usó la estrategia de la espera y bajo perfil |url=https://politica.expansion.mx/elecciones/2023/09/05/omar-garcia-harfuch-cdmx-estrategia |access-date=13 August 2024 |website=ADNPolítico |language=es}}</ref>

Sheinbaum also oversaw the gradual deployment of the National Guard in Mexico City. While some experts viewed the measure as a deterrent, others questioned its tangible impact on violent crime, suggesting it served more as a symbolic presence.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Olson |first=Georgina |date=4 July 2021 |title=CDMX tendrá 16 coordinaciones regionales de Guardia Nacional en 2021 |url=https://www.excelsior.com.mx/comunidad/cdmx-tendra-16-coordinaciones-regionales-de-guardia-nacional-en-2021/1458228 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210812180144/https://www.excelsior.com.mx/comunidad/cdmx-tendra-16-coordinaciones-regionales-de-guardia-nacional-en-2021/1458228 |archive-date=12 August 2021 |access-date=8 July 2024 |website=Excélsior |language=es-MX}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Pérez Ricart |first=Carlos |date=29 January 2024 |title=¿Por qué ha mejorado la percepción de seguridad en México? |url=https://www.milenio.com/opinion/carlos-perez-ricart/columna-carlos-perez-ricart/por-que-ha-mejorado-la-percepcion-de-seguridad-en-mexico |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240621235251/https://www.milenio.com/opinion/carlos-perez-ricart/columna-carlos-perez-ricart/por-que-ha-mejorado-la-percepcion-de-seguridad-en-mexico |archive-date=21 June 2024 |access-date=7 July 2024 |website=Milenio}}</ref>

=== Education ===
[[File:Claudia_Sheinbaum_(49503316651).jpg|thumb|upright|Claudia Sheinbaum in February 2020]]
As part of her administration's education policy, the {{lang|es|Mi Beca para Empezar}} ({{literal translation|My Scholarship to Get Started}}) scholarship program was created for 1.2 million students from preschool to secondary education and, in 2022, was elevated to constitutional law in Mexico City.<ref>{{Cite web |last=González Alvarado |first=Rocío |title=Aumenta 20% montos de Mi Beca para Empezar en CDMX |url=https://www.jornada.com.mx/notas/2023/05/01/capital/aumenta-20-montos-de-mi-beca-para-empezar-en-cdmx/ |access-date=19 June 2023 |website=www.jornada.com.mx |date=May 2023 |language=es |archive-date=19 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230619212534/https://www.jornada.com.mx/notas/2023/05/01/capital/aumenta-20-montos-de-mi-beca-para-empezar-en-cdmx/ |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Santiago |first=David |date=22 November 2022 |title=CDMX eleva a rango constitucional la beca "Bienestar" y "La Escuela Es Nuestra" |url=https://politica.expansion.mx/cdmx/2022/11/22/cdmx-eleva-a-rango-constitucional-la-beca-bienestar-y-la-escuela-es-nuestra |access-date=19 June 2023 |website=ADNPolítico |language=es |archive-date=19 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230619212558/https://politica.expansion.mx/cdmx/2022/11/22/cdmx-eleva-a-rango-constitucional-la-beca-bienestar-y-la-escuela-es-nuestra |url-status=live}}</ref> For higher education, the {{ill|Rosario Castellanos Institute of Higher Studies|lt=Rosario Castellanos Institute of Higher Studies|es|Universidad Rosario Castellanos}} and the University of Health were established.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Sheinbaum celebra reforma para que Instituto Rosario Castellanos sea Universidad |url=https://www.eluniversal.com.mx/metropoli/sheinbaum-celebra-reforma-para-que-instituto-rosario-castellanos-sea-universidad/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230619212532/https://www.eluniversal.com.mx/metropoli/sheinbaum-celebra-reforma-para-que-instituto-rosario-castellanos-sea-universidad/ |archive-date=19 June 2023 |access-date=19 June 2023 |website=El Universal |language=es}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=8 November 2019 |title=AMLO y Sheinbaum anuncian Universidad de la Salud |url=https://www.razon.com.mx/mexico/amlo-y-sheinbaum-anuncian-universidad-de-la-salud/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230622213053/https://www.razon.com.mx/mexico/amlo-y-sheinbaum-anuncian-universidad-de-la-salud/ |archive-date=22 June 2023 |access-date=19 June 2023 |website=La Razón |language=es}}</ref>

Community centers called {{lang|es|pilares}} ({{literal translation|pillars}}) were established in marginalized neighborhoods and towns.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Valencia |first=Frida |date=20 April 2023 |title=Claudia Sheinbaum inaugura el Pilares La Comuna" en Álvaro Obregón |url=https://heraldodemexico.com.mx/nacional/2023/4/20/claudia-sheinbaum-inaugura-el-pilares-la-comuna-en-alvaro-obregon-499352.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230619212542/https://heraldodemexico.com.mx/nacional/2023/4/20/claudia-sheinbaum-inaugura-el-pilares-la-comuna-en-alvaro-obregon-499352.html |archive-date=19 June 2023 |access-date=19 June 2023 |website=El Heraldo de México |language=es}}</ref> These spaces promoted arts, sports, education, and cultural activities and were recognized with an award from [[UNESCO]] in 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |date=7 January 2021 |title=Programa Pilares de la CDMX recibió premio de la Unesco |url=https://www.infobae.com/america/mexico/2021/01/07/programa-pilares-de-la-cdmx-recibio-premio-de-la-unesco/ |access-date=8 July 2024 |website=infobae |language=es-ES |archive-date=3 August 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240803163226/https://www.infobae.com/america/mexico/2021/01/07/programa-pilares-de-la-cdmx-recibio-premio-de-la-unesco/ |url-status=live}}</ref>

=== Environment ===
In June 2019, Sheinbaum announced a new six-year environmental plan to reduce [[air pollution]] by 30%, plant 15 million trees, ban [[single-use plastic]]s and promote [[recycling]], build a new [[waste separation]] plant, provide water service to every home, construct 100 kilometers of trolleybus and metrobús-only corridors, and construct and install solar panels and water heaters.<ref>{{cite web |date=6 June 2019 |title=In six years, water service for everyone: Mexico City mayor |url=https://mexiconewsdaily.com/news/in-six-years-water-service-for-everyone/ |access-date=29 April 2020 |publisher=Mexico News Daily |archive-date=17 August 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200817163035/https://mexiconewsdaily.com/news/in-six-years-water-service-for-everyone/ |url-status=live}}</ref>

=== Infrastructure ===

==== Public transportation ====
[[File:MX MM INAUGURACIÓN CABLEBÚS LÍNEA 1 - 17.jpg|thumb|Sheinbaum at the inauguration of Line 1 of the Cablebús]]
Sheinbaum introduced the [[Cablebús]] cable car system, with Lines 1 and 2 opening in 2021, and began construction on Line 3 the same year.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Navarrete |first=Shelma |date=8 August 2021 |title=Sheinbaum inaugura Cablebús en Iztapalapa entre porras y festejos en azoteas |url=https://politica.expansion.mx/cdmx/2021/08/08/sheinbaum-inaugura-cablebus-en-iztapalapa-entre-porras-y-festejos-en-azoteas |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230619212532/https://politica.expansion.mx/cdmx/2021/08/08/sheinbaum-inaugura-cablebus-en-iztapalapa-entre-porras-y-festejos-en-azoteas |archive-date=19 June 2023 |access-date=19 June 2023 |website=ADNPolítico |language=es}}</ref><ref name="El Heraldo de México-2022">{{Cite web |date=3 October 2022 |title=Claudia Sheinbaum resalta inversión histórica en movilidad para la CDMX |url=https://heraldodemexico.com.mx/nacional/2022/10/3/claudia-sheinbaum-resalta-inversion-historica-en-movilidad-para-la-cdmx-445089.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221003213459/https://heraldodemexico.com.mx/nacional/2022/10/3/claudia-sheinbaum-resalta-inversion-historica-en-movilidad-para-la-cdmx-445089.html |archive-date=3 October 2022 |access-date=8 July 2024 |website=El Heraldo de México |language=es}}</ref> Her administration expanded the Metrobús network by 33 kilometers, electrified Line 3, and added low-emission buses to the city’s ''[[Red de Transporte de Pasajeros]]''.''<ref name="El Heraldo de México-2022" />''<ref>{{Cite web |date=21 February 2023 |title=Línea 3 del Metrobús de la CDMX Ahora es 100% Eléctrica |url=https://www.nmas.com.mx/ciudad-de-mexico/linea-3-metrobus-cdmx-estrena-unidades-electricas/ |access-date=24 October 2024 |website=N+ |language=es-MX}}</ref>

She continued the extension of [[Mexico City Metro Line 12]] to [[Observatorio metro station (Mexico City)|Observatorio station]] and launched a MX$37 billion modernization of [[Mexico City Metro Line 1|Metro Line 1]] in 2022, including new trains, track replacements, and an upgraded control system.<ref>{{Cite web |date=27 June 2022 |title=Esto costará la modernización de la Línea 1 del Metro, según Sheinbaum |url=https://www.elfinanciero.com.mx/cdmx/2022/06/27/esto-costara-la-modernizacion-de-la-linea-1-del-metro-segun-sheinbaum/ |access-date=24 October 2024 |website=El Financiero |language=es}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |date=5 September 2019 |title=Mexico City announces 40-billion-peso modernization plan for Metro |url=https://mexiconewsdaily.com/news/40-billion-peso-modernization-plan-for-metro/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200817162029/https://mexiconewsdaily.com/news/40-billion-peso-modernization-plan-for-metro/ |archive-date=17 August 2020 |access-date=30 April 2020 |work=Mexico News Daily}}</ref> Her administration started Observatorio's redevelopment into a major terminal connecting Lines 1, 12, and the [[El Insurgente]] commuter rail line.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Vargas |first=Aabye |date=25 May 2022 |title=Inicia la renovación del Complejo Observatorio |url=https://www.elsoldemexico.com.mx/metropoli/cdmx/inicia-la-renovacion-del-complejo-observatorio-8333434.html |access-date=24 October 2024 |website=El Sol de México |language=es}}</ref>

Her government introduced a unified mobility card for all public transit systems and expanded cycling infrastructure with 200 kilometers of bike lanes and 2,500 new [[Ecobici (Mexico City)|Ecobici]] bikes.''<ref name="El Heraldo de México-2022" />''<ref>{{Cite web |title=Claudia Sheinbaum presenta 'Movilidad Integrada', nueva red integral de transporte público |url=https://www.elgrafico.mx/al-dia/claudia-sheinbaum-presenta-movilidad-integrada-nueva-red-integral-de-transporte-publico |access-date=24 October 2024 |website=www.elgrafico.mx |language=es}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=10 November 2022 |title=CDMX impulsa la movilidad integrada |url=https://www.imagenradio.com.mx/cdmx-impulsa-la-movilidad-integrada |access-date=24 October 2024 |website=Imagen Radio 90.5 |language=es-MX}}</ref>

==== Roads and highways ====
Sheinbaum announced the construction of vehicular bridges to improve road connectivity. Three notable projects included the Cuemanco Bridge, which connected Periférico Oriente with [[Canal Nacional]]; a new junction linking [[Circuito Interior]] with [[Eje vial|Eje 6]]; and Las Adelitas Bridge, which connected Circuito Interior with Gran Canal.<ref>{{Cite web |date=4 September 2021 |title=Claudia Sheinbaum entrega nuevo puente vehicular en Xochimilco |url=https://heraldodemexico.com.mx/nacional/2021/9/4/claudia-sheinbaum-entrega-nuevo-puente-vehicular-en-xochimilco-332312.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211021040503/https://heraldodemexico.com.mx/nacional/2021/9/4/claudia-sheinbaum-entrega-nuevo-puente-vehicular-en-xochimilco-332312.html |archive-date=21 October 2021 |access-date=8 July 2024 |website=El Heraldo de México |language=es}}</ref>

==== Criticism ====
Sheinbaum faced criticism for the management of the budget allocated to public transportation. Although she claimed that there were no cuts and that resources for the Metro were increased, budget data showed fluctuations in the allocation of funds for different transportation systems between 2018 and 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Tapia |first=Anayeli |date=13 January 2023 |title=Sin control y con menos recursos, el transporte de la CDMX se convierte en la piedra en el zapato de Claudia Sheinbaum |url=https://www.infobae.com/america/mexico/2023/01/13/sin-control-y-con-menos-recursos-el-transporte-de-la-cdmx-se-convierte-en-la-piedra-en-el-zapato-de-claudia-sheinbaum/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240803163223/https://www.infobae.com/america/mexico/2023/01/13/sin-control-y-con-menos-recursos-el-transporte-de-la-cdmx-se-convierte-en-la-piedra-en-el-zapato-de-claudia-sheinbaum/ |archive-date=3 August 2024 |access-date=8 July 2024 |website=infobae |language=es-ES}}</ref>

Other infrastructure projects, such as the renovation of Mexico City Metro Line 1, the extension of Mexico City Metro Line 12 to Observatorio, the construction of the Interurban Train Mexico City–Toluca, and Line 3 of the Cablebús, remained incomplete at the time of her resignation to seek her party's presidential nomination.<ref>{{Cite web |date=18 June 2023 |title=Un gobierno de contrastes: así fue el paso de Claudia Sheinbaum por la CDMX |url=https://animalpolitico.com/politica/gobierno-contrastes-claudia-sheinbaum-cdmx |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240604170833/https://animalpolitico.com/politica/gobierno-contrastes-claudia-sheinbaum-cdmx |archive-date=4 June 2024 |access-date=8 July 2024 |website=Animal Politico |language=en}}</ref>

=== Social issues ===
In 2019, Sheinbaum implemented a gender-neutral uniform policy for students in state-run schools, allowing them to wear uniforms of their choice regardless of gender.<ref>{{Cite news |date=4 June 2019 |title=Mexico City unveils gender-neutral school uniforms policy |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-mexico-lgbt-uniforms-idUSKCN1T512Q |access-date=7 September 2023 |work=Reuters |language=en |archive-date=7 September 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230907173812/https://www.reuters.com/article/us-mexico-lgbt-uniforms-idUSKCN1T512Q |url-status=live}}</ref> In 2021, Sheinbaum removed a statue of [[Christopher Columbus]] from Mexico City's [[Paseo de la Reforma]] as part of what she called a "[[decolonization]]" exercise.<ref>{{Cite news |date=6 September 2021 |title=Mexico City to replace Columbus statue with one of indigenous woman |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/mexico-city-replace-columbus-statue-central-avenue-2021-09-06/ |access-date=26 September 2023 |work=Reuters |language=en |archive-date=11 October 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231011183554/https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/mexico-city-replace-columbus-statue-central-avenue-2021-09-06/ |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=13 October 2021 |title=Mexico City to swap Columbus statue for one of indigenous woman |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/world-latin-america-58893051 |access-date=26 September 2023 |work=BBC News |language=en-GB |archive-date=13 July 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230713200904/https://www.bbc.com/news/world-latin-america-58893051 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Mexico City swapping Columbus statue with one of Indigenous woman |url=https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/9/6/mexico-city-swapping-columbus-statue-one-indigenous-woman |access-date=26 September 2023 |website=www.aljazeera.com |language=en |archive-date=4 October 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231004011253/https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/9/6/mexico-city-swapping-columbus-statue-one-indigenous-woman |url-status=live}}</ref>

=== Crisis management ===
==== COVID-19 pandemic response ====
[[File:MX MR ENCENDIDO 500 AÑOS 17.jpg|thumb|Sheinbaum during the COVID-19 pandemic on 12 August 2021]]
Shortly after the first [[COVID-19 pandemic in Mexico|COVID-19 case in Mexico City]] was confirmed on 28 February 2020, Sheinbaum addressed the city, emphasizing that although the risk was low, the population needed to stay informed through official sources.<ref>{{Cite web |date=28 February 2020 |title=Claudia Sheinbaum pidió calma y solidaridad por alta probabilidad de coronavirus en CDMX: "Estamos preparados" |url=https://www.infobae.com/america/mexico/2020/02/28/claudia-sheinbaum-pidio-calma-y-solidaridad-por-alta-probabilidad-de-coronavirus-en-cdmx-estamos-preparados/ |access-date=2 June 2024 |website=infobae |language=es-ES |archive-date=2 June 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240602080255/https://www.infobae.com/america/mexico/2020/02/28/claudia-sheinbaum-pidio-calma-y-solidaridad-por-alta-probabilidad-de-coronavirus-en-cdmx-estamos-preparados/ |url-status=live}}</ref> On 19 March, Sheinbaum urged residents to stay at home to prevent the spread of infection. She also advised those with symptoms to text a hotline for guidance instead of going to hospitals to avoid overwhelming the healthcare system.<ref>{{Cite web |date=20 March 2020 |title=Sheinbaum pide a capitalinos quedarse en casa para evitar contagios |url=https://politica.expansion.mx/cdmx/2020/03/20/sheinbaum-pide-a-capitalinos-quedarse-en-casa-para-evitar-contagios |access-date=2 June 2024 |website=ADNPolítico |language=es |archive-date=2 June 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240602080236/https://politica.expansion.mx/cdmx/2020/03/20/sheinbaum-pide-a-capitalinos-quedarse-en-casa-para-evitar-contagios |url-status=live}}</ref> On 22 March, Sheinbaum announced the closure of commercial establishments, cultural venues, sports facilities, and religious spaces.<ref>{{Cite web |date=23 March 2020 |title=Claudia Sheinbaum inició de manera oficial la campaña contra el coronavirus "Quédate en casa" |url=https://www.infobae.com/america/mexico/2020/03/23/claudia-sheinbaum-inicio-de-manera-oficial-la-campana-contra-el-coronavirus-quedate-en-casa/ |access-date=2 June 2024 |website=infobae |language=es-ES |archive-date=2 June 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240602080237/https://www.infobae.com/america/mexico/2020/03/23/claudia-sheinbaum-inicio-de-manera-oficial-la-campana-contra-el-coronavirus-quedate-en-casa/ |url-status=live}}</ref>

López Obrador and Sheinbaum had differing views on using face masks: Sheinbaum encouraged Mexico City residents to wear [[Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic|face masks]], while López Obrador frequently did not wear them in public.<ref>{{Cite web |title=AMLO tiene sus razones para no usar cubrebocas; en CDMX, pensamos que sí es importante: Sheinbaum |url=https://aristeguinoticias.com/0902/mexico/amlo-tiene-sus-razones-para-no-usar-cubrebocas-en-cdmx-pensamos-que-si-es-importante-sheinbaum/ |access-date=2 June 2024 |website=Aristegui Noticias |language=es |archive-date=2 June 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240602080236/https://aristeguinoticias.com/0902/mexico/amlo-tiene-sus-razones-para-no-usar-cubrebocas-en-cdmx-pensamos-que-si-es-importante-sheinbaum/ |url-status=live}}</ref> During her administration, over 200,000 kits containing [[Ivermectin during the COVID-19 pandemic|ivermectin]] were distributed to patients diagnosed with COVID-19 without their knowledge.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/2022/02/09/mexico-city-covid-ivermectin/|title=Mexico City gave ivermectin to thousands of covid patients. Officials face an ethics backlash|date=9 February 2022|newspaper=[[The Washington Post]]|first=Mary Beth|last=Sheridan|access-date=19 July 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.elpasotimes.com/story/news/politics/2024/10/01/mexicos-new-president-claudia-sheinbaum-faces-many-challenges/75442728007/|title=Mexico's new president Claudia Sheinbaum faces many challenges|first1=Eduardo|last1=Garcia|first2=Alfredo|last2=Corchado|date=1 October 2024|location=[[Mexico City]]|access-date=19 July 2025|newspaper=[[El Paso Times]]}}</ref>

Sheinbaum was nominated by the [[City Mayors Foundation]] for the [[World Mayor]] Prize in 2021 in [[North America]] for her handling of the COVID-19 pandemic in Mexico.<ref>{{cite news |date=30 March 2021 |title=Nominan a Sheinbaum como mejor alcaldesa del mundo por manejo de la pandemia |url=https://aristeguinoticias.com/3003/mexico/nominan-a-sheinbaum-como-mejor-alcaldesa-del-mundo-por-manejo-de-la-pandemia/ |access-date=3 April 2021 |work=Aristegui Noticias |language=es |archive-date=31 March 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210331013344/https://aristeguinoticias.com/3003/mexico/nominan-a-sheinbaum-como-mejor-alcaldesa-del-mundo-por-manejo-de-la-pandemia/ |url-status=live}}</ref>

==== Collapse of Line 12 of the Mexico City Metro ====
{{Main|Mexico City Metro overpass collapse}}
[[File:Incidente Línea 12 Ciudad México 2021.jpg|thumb|Investigators at the collapse site]]
At around 10:22&nbsp;p.m. on 3 May 2021, several girders, part of the tracks, and two wagons of Line 12 of the Mexico City Metro collapsed between the [[Olivos metro station|Olivos]] and [[Tezonco metro station|Tezonco]] stations. The casualties were 26 dead, 80 injured, and five missing. Line 12 of the Metro had been inaugurated on 30 October 2012 by the head of government of Mexico City, [[Marcelo Ebrard]], and the president of Mexico, [[Felipe Calderón]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Con Calderón y Ebrard en la ceremonia: así fue la inauguración de la Línea 12 del Metro en 2012 |url=https://www.infobae.com/america/mexico/2021/05/04/con-calderon-y-ebrard-en-la-ceremonia-asi-fue-la-inauguracion-de-la-linea-12-del-metro-en-2012/ |access-date=3 June 2024 |agency=Infobae |date=4 May 2021 |archive-date=28 January 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230128132700/https://www.infobae.com/america/mexico/2021/05/04/con-calderon-y-ebrard-en-la-ceremonia-asi-fue-la-inauguracion-de-la-linea-12-del-metro-en-2012/ |url-status=live}}</ref>

Engineering flaws that had existed prior to the line's inauguration became worse over time, necessitating maintenance repairs over the next three years, including an unprecedented [[Mexico City Metro Line 12#Temporary partial closure|closure of the line]] to re-shape some sections of tracks and to replace the rails; most of these improvements were carried out during the term of [[Miguel Ángel Mancera]] as Head of Government. On 4 May 2021, Ebrard, then serving as [[Secretary of Foreign Affairs (Mexico)|Secretary of Foreign Affairs]], said that the work was definitively delivered in July 2013, after reviews carried out for seven months, and expressed his willingness to respond and collaborate in the event of any request from the authorities.<ref>{{cite web |date=4 May 2021 |title=Ebrard da la cara tras accidente en Metro. El que nada debe nada teme: Ebrard sobre accidente en L12 del Metro |url=https://www.milenio.com/politica/metro-el-que-nada-debe-nada-teme-dice-ebrard-sobre-accidente-en-l12 |access-date=28 December 2021 |language=es |newspaper=Milenio Diario |archive-date=28 December 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211228214647/https://www.milenio.com/politica/metro-el-que-nada-debe-nada-teme-dice-ebrard-sobre-accidente-en-l12 |url-status=live}}</ref>

[[Det Norske Veritas]] (DNV), a Norwegian company in charge of investigating the causes of the collapse of Metro Line 12, detected that one of the beams that collapsed already had structural failures since before the earthquake of 19 September 2017, a factor that had caused problems in the elevated section of the line that collapsed.<ref>{{cite web |date=7 September 2021 |title=Tenían fallas vigas de la L12 del metro desde antes del sismo del 17; culpa apunta hacia Marcelo Ebrard y Mario Delgado |url=https://democratacoahuila.com/2021/09/07/tenian-fallas-vigas-de-la-l12-del-metro-desde-antes-del-sismo-del-17-culpa-apunta-hacia-marcelo-ebrard-y-mario-delgado/ |access-date=28 December 2021 |language=es |newspaper=El Demócrata. Primer diario digital de Coahuila |archive-date=28 December 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211228214639/https://democratacoahuila.com/2021/09/07/tenian-fallas-vigas-de-la-l12-del-metro-desde-antes-del-sismo-del-17-culpa-apunta-hacia-marcelo-ebrard-y-mario-delgado/ |url-status=live}}</ref> On 28 June 2021, Sheinbaum dismissed the general director of the Mexico City Metro, {{ill|Florencia Serranía Soto|es|Florencia Serranía Soto}}.<ref>{{cite web |author=Elías Camhaji |date=28 June 2021 |title=Sheinbaum deja caer a la jefa del metro de Ciudad de México casi dos meses después del colapso de la Línea 12 |url=https://elpais.com/mexico/2021-06-28/florencia-serrania-deja-la-direccion-del-metro-de-ciudad-de-mexico.html |access-date=28 December 2021 |language=es |newspaper=El País |archive-date=8 October 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211008173023/https://elpais.com/mexico/2021-06-28/florencia-serrania-deja-la-direccion-del-metro-de-ciudad-de-mexico.html |url-status=live}}</ref>

Some political observers suggested that the political fallout from the disaster could harm Sheinbaum's [[candidacy]] in the 2024 presidential election.<ref>{{Cite news |last1=Abi-Habib |first1=Maria |last2=Lopez |first2=Oscar |date=4 May 2021 |title=The political fallout enveloped two top presidential contenders. |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2021/05/04/world/americas/mexico-city-train-crash-claudia-sheinbaum-mayors.html |access-date=17 August 2021 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331 |archive-date=17 August 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210817220423/https://www.nytimes.com/2021/05/04/world/americas/mexico-city-train-crash-claudia-sheinbaum-mayors.html |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=5 May 2021 |title=Analysis: Rail accident rattles Mexico's presidential succession favorites |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/rail-accident-rattles-mexicos-presidential-succession-favorites-2021-05-05/ |access-date=17 August 2021 |website=Reuters |language=en |archive-date=17 August 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210817220604/https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/rail-accident-rattles-mexicos-presidential-succession-favorites-2021-05-05/ |url-status=live}}</ref> Alejo Sánchez Cano, editor of the Mexico City daily newspaper {{lang|es|[[El Financiero]]}}, opined that Sheinbaum's responsibility was unavoidable, stating that after having been in office for two and a half years, she failed to maintain the Metro system.<ref>{{cite web |author=Alejo Sánchez Cano |date=18 June 2021 |title=La Línea 12 no volverá a funcionar en la administración de Sheinbaum |url=https://www.elfinanciero.com.mx/opinion/alejo-sanchez-cano/2021/06/17/la-linea-12-no-volvera-a-funcionar-en-la-administracion-de-sheinbaum/ |access-date=28 December 2021 |language=es |newspaper=El Financiero |archive-date=28 December 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211228214638/https://www.elfinanciero.com.mx/opinion/alejo-sanchez-cano/2021/06/17/la-linea-12-no-volvera-a-funcionar-en-la-administracion-de-sheinbaum/ |url-status=live}}</ref>

== 2024 presidential campaign ==
=== Nomination ===
[[File:Claudia Sheinbaum precandidata presidencial.jpg|thumb|left|Sheinbaum receiving a certificate confirming her as the presidential nominee for ''Sigamos Haciendo Historia'' on 19 November 2023]]

On 12 June 2023, Sheinbaum announced that she would resign as head of government of Mexico City on 16 June to contend in the internal selection process to select a ''[[de facto]]'' presidential candidate for ''Juntos Hacemos Historia'', a coalition encompassing Morena, the Labor Party, and the [[Ecologist Green Party of Mexico]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Sánchez |first1=Fabiola |date=12 June 2023 |title=Mexico's top diplomat resigns to enter primary race for 2024 presidential election |url=https://apnews.com/article/mexico-presidential-primary-morena-resignations-331d292e5a1e84dd962ebb94181b445c |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230612213442/https://apnews.com/article/mexico-presidential-primary-morena-resignations-331d292e5a1e84dd962ebb94181b445c |archive-date=12 June 2023 |access-date=12 June 2023 |publisher=[[Associated Press]]|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Zerega |first1=Georgina |date=12 June 2023 |title=Claudia Sheinbaum dejará su cargo el 16 de junio para ser 'la primera mujer en encabezar los destinos' de México |trans-title=Claudia Sheinbaum will leave her post the 16th of June to become 'the first woman to lead the fate of the nation' of Mexico |url=https://elpais.com/mexico/2023-06-12/claudia-sheinbaum-anuncia-que-dejara-el-gobierno-de-ciudad-de-mexico-el-16-de-junio-para-entrar-en-la-interna-de-morena.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230613022552/https://elpais.com/mexico/2023-06-12/claudia-sheinbaum-anuncia-que-dejara-el-gobierno-de-ciudad-de-mexico-el-16-de-junio-para-entrar-en-la-interna-de-morena.html |archive-date=13 June 2023 |access-date=13 June 2023 |website=[[El País]] |language=es}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |date=12 June 2023 |title=Mexico City mayor to step down to pursue historic bid for presidency |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/mexico-city-mayor-step-down-pursue-historic-bid-presidency-2023-06-12/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230612215646/https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/mexico-city-mayor-step-down-pursue-historic-bid-presidency-2023-06-12/ |archive-date=12 June 2023 |access-date=13 June 2023 |publisher=[[Reuters]] |language=en}}</ref> Speculation regarding her nationality emerged after former president [[Vicente Fox]] referred to her as a "Bulgarian Jew". In response, Sheinbaum released her birth certificate, showing she was born in Mexico City.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Romero |first1=Simon |last2=Kitreoff |first2=Natalie |date=3 June 2024 |title=Claudia Sheinbaum es la primera persona judía en llegar a la presidencia en México |url=https://www.nytimes.com/es/2024/06/03/espanol/claudia-sheinbaum-judia-presidente-mexico.html?searchResultPosition=1 |work=The New York Times}}</ref>

The coalition's internal process consisted of five polls from 28 August to 4 September.
