On 6 September, Sheinbaum was declared the winner, securing 39.38% of the vote and defeating her closest opponent, former foreign secretary Marcelo Ebrard, by around 13 points.<ref name="ABC News-2023" /> On 19 November 2023, Sheinbaum was registered as the presidential nominee of ''[[Sigamos Haciendo Historia]]'', the successor coalition to ''Juntos Hacemos Historia''.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/en-espanol/noticias/mexico/articulo/2023-11-19/claudia-sheinbaum-se-registra-como-precandidata-presidencial-del-partido-de-lopez-obrador|title=Claudia Sheinbaum se registra como precandidata presidencial del partido de López Obrador|publisher=[[EFE]]|via=[[The San Diego Union-Tribune]]|date=19 November 2023|access-date=4 June 2024|archive-date=2 December 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231202184223/https://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/en-espanol/noticias/mexico/articulo/2023-11-19/claudia-sheinbaum-se-registra-como-precandidata-presidencial-del-partido-de-lopez-obrador|url-status=live}}</ref> Sheinbaum formally registered her candidacy at the [[National Electoral Institute]] (INE) on 18 February 2024.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.barrons.com/news/pre-election-protests-in-mexico-as-ex-mayor-joins-presidential-race-f34aef85|title=Pre-election Protests In Mexico As Ex-mayor Joins Presidential Race|last=Arce|first=Jean|date=18 February 2024|newspaper=[[Barron's]]|access-date=4 June 2024|archive-date=21 February 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240221064647/https://www.barrons.com/news/pre-election-protests-in-mexico-as-ex-mayor-joins-presidential-race-f34aef85|url-status=live}}</ref>

=== General election ===
{{Main|2024 Mexican general election}}

[[File:Inicio de campaña de Claudia Sheinbaum.jpg|thumb|Sheinbaum at the start of her campaign in the Zócalo of Mexico City on 1 March 2024]]

On 1 March 2024, Sheinbaum launched her campaign at the [[Zócalo]], outlining her proposals and emphasizing her commitment to continuing President López Obrador's [[Fourth Transformation]] policies.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Oré |first1=Diego |last2=Barrera |first2=Adriana |date=1 March 2024 |title=Mexico kicks off election campaign with ruling party's Sheinbaum in lead |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/mexico-kicks-off-election-campaign-with-ruling-partys-sheinbaum-lead-2024-03-01/ |access-date=4 June 2024 |publisher=[[Reuters]]}}</ref> She pledged to pass "Plan C", a package of eighteen constitutional amendments proposed by López Obrador earlier that year, which include increasing the minimum wage above inflation, elevating social programs to constitutional law, and [[2024 Mexican judicial reform|electing judiciary members by popular vote]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=López |first=Alejandro I. |date=6 February 2024 |title=Las 20 reformas constitucionales que propone López Obrador |url=https://elpais.com/mexico/2024-02-06/las-20-reformas-constitucionales-que-propone-lopez-obrador.html |access-date=7 June 2024 |website=El País México |language=es |archive-date=2 March 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240302183146/https://elpais.com/mexico/2024-02-06/las-20-reformas-constitucionales-que-propone-lopez-obrador.html |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=1 March 2024 |title=Con el 72% del país gobernado por Morena, Sheinbaum busca 35 millones de votos que la lleven a la Presidencia |url=https://animalpolitico.com/elecciones-2024/presidencia/sheinbaum-morena-busca-35-millones-votos |access-date=7 June 2024 |website=Animal Politico |language=en |archive-date=2 April 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240402045856/https://animalpolitico.com/elecciones-2024/presidencia/sheinbaum-morena-busca-35-millones-votos |url-status=live}}</ref> She also proposed replicating her Mexico City security strategy nationwide, introducing a constitutional amendment to prevent reelection for any popularly elected position, and implementing new social programs for students from [[preschool]] to [[secondary education]] and women aged 60 to 64.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Terreros |first=Brenda |date=2 March 2024 |title=Estos son los 100 compromisos de Claudia Sheinbaum al inicio de su campaña |url=https://www.infobae.com/mexico/2024/03/02/estos-son-los-100-compromisos-de-claudia-sheinbaum-al-inicio-de-su-campana/ |access-date=7 June 2024 |website=infobae |language=es |archive-date=7 June 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240607222626/https://www.infobae.com/mexico/2024/03/02/estos-son-los-100-compromisos-de-claudia-sheinbaum-al-inicio-de-su-campana/ |url-status=live}}</ref>

During debates and the campaign, Sheinbaum was accused by [[Xóchitl Gálvez]], the candidate from the opposition coalition ''[[Fuerza y Corazón por México]]'', of being responsible for the collapse of the Colegio Rébsamen during the 2017 Puebla earthquake, the [[Mexico City Metro overpass collapse]], and the excess deaths during the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Mexico City]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=7 April 2024 |title=Así le hemos contado el primer debate presidencial |url=https://elpais.com/mexico/elecciones-mexicanas/2024-04-07/primer-debate-presidencial-en-mexico-2024-en-vivo.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240408101824/https://elpais.com/mexico/elecciones-mexicanas/2024-04-07/primer-debate-presidencial-en-mexico-2024-en-vivo.html |archive-date=8 April 2024 |access-date=8 April 2024 |website=El País México |language=es}}</ref>

[[File:Claudia Sheinbaum discurso de la victoria.jpg|thumb|Sheinbaum during her victory speech on 2 June 2024]]
[[Opinion polling for the 2024 Mexican general election|Polls consistently indicated]] that Sheinbaum held a substantial lead over her main opponent, Xóchitl Gálvez.<ref>{{Cite news |last1=Romero |first1=Simon |last2=Mega |first2=Emiliano Rodríguez |date=1 March 2024 |title=Why Mexico's Ruling Party Candidate Is Already Dominating the Presidential Race |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2024/03/01/world/americas/mexico-election-amlo-sheinbaum-galvez.html |access-date=3 June 2024 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331 |archive-date=2 June 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240602160954/https://www.nytimes.com/2024/03/01/world/americas/mexico-election-amlo-sheinbaum-galvez.html |url-status=live}}</ref> During the [[2024 Mexican general election#Debates|three presidential debates]], many commentators praised her calm demeanor during provocations from Gálvez.<ref>{{Cite web |date=8 April 2024 |title=¿Quién ha ganado el primer debate presidencial? Siete expertos dan su veredicto |url=https://elpais.com/mexico/elecciones-mexicanas/2024-04-08/quien-ha-ganado-el-debate-siete-expertos-dan-su-veredicto.html |access-date=7 June 2024 |website=El País México |language=es |archive-date=8 April 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240408101825/https://elpais.com/mexico/elecciones-mexicanas/2024-04-08/quien-ha-ganado-el-debate-siete-expertos-dan-su-veredicto.html |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Esquivel |first=Karen |date=20 May 2024 |title=ANÁLISIS: ¿Quién ganó y quien perdió el tercer debate presidencial de México entre Sheinbaum, Gálvez y Máynez? |url=https://cnnespanol.cnn.com/2024/05/20/analisis-quien-gano-tercer-debate-presidencial-mexico-elecciones-orix/ |access-date=7 June 2024 |website=CNN |language=es |archive-date=20 May 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240520130944/https://cnnespanol.cnn.com/2024/05/20/analisis-quien-gano-tercer-debate-presidencial-mexico-elecciones-orix/ |url-status=live}}</ref>

The election took place on 2 June 2024, with Sheinbaum being projected the winner by the INE's quick count at 11:50 CST, making her the virtual president-elect.<ref name="nyt-results">{{cite news |last1=Beltran |first1=Gray |last2=Lemonides |first2=Alex |last3=Bloch |first3=Matthew |last4=González Gómez |first4=Martín |title=Mexico Election Results: Sheinbaum Wins |url=https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2024/06/02/world/americas/results-mexico-presidential-election.html |access-date=3 June 2024 |work=[[The New York Times]] |date=2 June 2024 |archive-date=3 June 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240603004330/https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2024/06/02/world/americas/results-mexico-presidential-election.html |url-status=live}}</ref> On 6 June, district tallies confirmed that Sheinbaum won a [[landslide victory]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ramírez |first=Leonardo |date=7 June 2024 |title=Claudia Sheinbaum gana elección con 59.75% de los votos, confirman Cómputos Distritales |url=https://www.ejecentral.com.mx/category/nuestro-eje/claudia-sheinbaum-gana-eleccion-con-59-75-de-los-votos-confirman-computos-distritales |access-date=7 June 2024 |website=Eje Central |language=es |archive-date=7 June 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240607222625/https://www.ejecentral.com.mx/category/nuestro-eje/claudia-sheinbaum-gana-eleccion-con-59-75-de-los-votos-confirman-computos-distritales |url-status=live}}</ref> She received the highest number of votes ever recorded for a candidate in Mexican history, carried 31 out of 32 states, and achieved 59.76% of the vote, the highest vote percentage since free and fair elections began in Mexico.<ref>{{Cite web |date=3 June 2024 |title=Claudia Sheinbaum: 3 números que muestran la magnitud de su victoria (y por qué puede llegar a tener más poder que AMLO) |url=https://www.bbc.com/mundo/articles/cg33ylzwgdgo |access-date=3 June 2024 |website=BBC News Mundo |language=es |archive-date=3 June 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240603125052/https://www.bbc.com/mundo/articles/cg33ylzwgdgo |url-status=live}}</ref>

=== Presidential transition ===
[[File:Claudia Sheinbaum presidenta electa.jpg|thumb|Sheinbaum during an event to celebrate her declaration as president-elect of Mexico on 15 August 2024]]
Following her victory, Sheinbaum met with President López Obrador to outline the presidential transition and her legislative agenda for the early months of her administration.<ref>{{Cite web |date=10 June 2024 |title=AMLO y Sheinbaum se reúnen en Palacio Nacional para arrancar el proceso de transición |url=https://www.eleconomista.com.mx/politica/AMLOy-Sheinbaum-se-reunen-en-Palacio-Nacional-para-arrancar-el-proceso-de-transicion-20240610-0063.html |access-date=12 August 2024 |website=El Economista}}</ref> She detailed that her priorities included new social programs for primary school students and women aged 60 to 64, modifications to the pension system for government employees, and a ban on reelection for any popularly elected position.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rojas |first=Arturo |date=11 June 2024 |title=Cambios al PJF y becas, prioridades en nuevo Congreso |url=https://www.eleconomista.com.mx/politica/Cambios-al-PJF-y-becas-prioridades-en-nuevo-Congreso-20240611-0009.html |access-date=12 August 2024 |website=El Economista}}</ref> While Sheinbaum voiced support for López Obrador's judicial reform, she agreed to open nine discussion forums to address its most controversial aspects.<ref>{{Cite web |date=11 June 2024 |title=Sheinbaum y legisladores de Morena acuerdan abrir diálogo nacional sobre la reforma al Poder Judicial |url=https://latinus.us/eleccion-2024/2024/6/11/sheinbaum-legisladores-de-morena-acuerdan-abrir-dialogo-nacional-sobre-la-reforma-al-poder-judicial-117175.html |access-date=12 August 2024 |website=LatinUS |language=es}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Aguilar Esquivel |first=Israel |date=25 June 2024 |title=Este es el calendario y los temas de los Diálogos para la Reforma del Poder Judicial |url=https://www.infobae.com/mexico/2024/06/25/este-es-el-calendario-y-los-temas-de-los-dialogos-para-la-reforma-del-poder-judicial/ |access-date=12 August 2024 |website=infobae |language=es-ES}}</ref>

Sheinbaum rolled out her cabinet appointments in phases, beginning with the first announcements on 20 June.<ref>{{cite news |author1=Alma E. Muñoz |author2=Georgina Saldierna |title=Anuncia Sheinbaum a seis integrantes de su gabinete |url=https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2024/06/20/politica/anuncia-sheinbaum-a-integrantes-de-su-gabinete-9799 |access-date=20 June 2024 |work=[[La Jornada]] |date=20 June 2024 |language=es |archive-date=20 June 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240620175659/https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2024/06/20/politica/anuncia-sheinbaum-a-integrantes-de-su-gabinete-9799 |url-status=live}}</ref> In early August, she met with governors and governors-elect to outline key projects for her 2025 budget.<ref>{{Cite web |last=López-Castro |first=Fernanda |date=6 August 2024 |title=Sheinbaum se reúne con segundo bloque de gobernadores del norte de México en CDMX |url=https://www.infobae.com/mexico/2024/08/06/sheinbaum-se-reune-con-segundo-bloque-de-gobernadores-del-noreste-de-mexico-en-cdmx/ |access-date=12 August 2024 |website=infobae |language=es-ES}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Claudia Sheinbaum se reúne con gobernadores del centro del país |url=https://www.eluniversal.com.mx/nacion/claudia-sheinbaum-se-reune-con-gobernadores-del-centro-del-pais/ |access-date=12 August 2024 |website=El Universal |language=es}}</ref> Sheinbaum also pledged to continue López Obrador's morning press conferences, known as ''mañaneras'', at 7:00 AM [[Central Time Zone|CST]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Las conferencias mañaneras seguirán con Sheinbaum a las 7:00 horas en Palacio Nacional |url=https://www.proceso.com.mx/nacional/2024/8/12/las-conferencias-mananeras-seguiran-con-sheinbaum-las-700-horas-en-palacio-nacional-334733.html |access-date=12 August 2024 |website=www.proceso.com.mx |language=spanish}}</ref>

After the [[LXVI Legislature of the Mexican Congress|LXVI Legislature]] was sworn in on 1 September, several of her campaign promises that stemmed from López Obrador's "Plan C" were either fully or partially passed by [[Congress of the Union|Congress]]. The judicial reform and the transfer of the [[National Guard (Mexico)|National Guard]] to the [[Secretariat of National Defense]] were passed by both chambers,<ref>{{Cite web |date=25 September 2024 |title=Senado aprueba en lo general y particular pase de la Guardia Nacional a Sedena... con voto de Yunes |url=https://www.elfinanciero.com.mx/nacional/2024/09/24/minuto-a-minuto-de-discusion-sobre-la-guardia-nacional-en-el-senado-hoy-24-de-septiembre/ |access-date=27 September 2024 |website=El Financiero |language=es}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Raziel |first=Zedryk |date=11 September 2024 |title=México aprueba la controvertida reforma judicial que somete al voto popular la elección de jueces |url=https://elpais.com/mexico/2024-09-11/mexico-aprueba-la-reforma-judicial-que-somete-al-voto-popular-la-eleccion-de-jueces.html |access-date=27 September 2024 |website=El País México |language=es-MX}}</ref> while the increases in the minimum wage above inflation and the elevation of certain social programs to constitutional status were approved solely by the [[Chamber of Deputies (Mexico)|Chamber of Deputies]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=26 September 2024 |title=Diputados elevan Jóvenes Construyendo el Futuro a rango constitucional |url=https://www.elfinanciero.com.mx/nacional/2024/09/26/diputados-elevan-jovenes-construyendo-el-futuro-a-rango-constitucional/ |access-date=27 September 2024 |website=El Financiero |language=es}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=25 September 2024 |title=Reforma al salario mínimo: Diputados aprueban iniciativa para que nunca esté debajo de la inflación |url=https://www.elfinanciero.com.mx/nacional/2024/09/24/reforma-al-salario-minimo-diputados-aprueban-iniciativa-para-que-nunca-este-debajo-de-la-inflacion/ |access-date=27 September 2024 |website=El Financiero |language=es}}</ref>

== Presidency (2024–present) ==
{{Progressivism sidebar|politicians}}
{{Main|Presidency of Claudia Sheinbaum}}

=== Inauguration ===
[[File:01.10.2024 - Cerimônia de transmissão do Poder Executivo Federal (54034977462).jpg|thumb|Andrés Manuel López Obrador hands the presidential sash to Ifigenia Martínez, who then presents it to Sheinbaum during her inauguration on 1 October 2024.]]
Sheinbaum was sworn in as president on 1 October 2024, becoming the first woman, as well as the first person with Jewish heritage,{{efn|[[Carlos Salinas de Gortari]], president of Mexico from 1988 to 1994, is of partial colonial-era Sephardic Jewish descent.<ref>{{cite web |title=Salinas de Gortari obtuvo nacionalidad española por origen judío sefaradí |url=https://www.enlacejudio.com/2022/10/30/salinas-de-gortari-obtuvo-nacionalidad-espanola-por-origen-judio-sefaradi/ |website=Enlace Judío |access-date=4 June 2024 |language=es-MX |date=30 October 2022 |archive-date=5 June 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240605025836/https://www.enlacejudio.com/2022/10/30/salinas-de-gortari-obtuvo-nacionalidad-espanola-por-origen-judio-sefaradi/ |url-status=live}}</ref>}} to hold the office.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.nbcnews.com/news/latino/claudia-sheinbaum-inauguration-mexico-first-female-president-rcna173325|title=Claudia Sheinbaum sworn in as Mexico's first female president in historic inauguration|first=Nicole|last=Acevedo|publisher=NBC News|date=1 October 2024|access-date=1 October 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/sheinbaum-sworn-mexicos-first-woman-president-2024-10-01/|title=Sheinbaum sworn in as Mexico's first woman president|publisher=Reuters|date=1 October 2024|access-date=1 October 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Buschschlüter |first1=Vanessa |date=3 June 2024 |title=Mexico elects Claudia Sheinbaum as first female president |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cp4475gwny1o |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240619035325/https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cp4475gwny1o |archive-date=19 June 2024 |access-date=20 June 2024 |agency=BBC News}}</ref> The presidential sash was handed to her by [[Ifigenia Martínez]], the [[President of the Chamber of Deputies (Mexico)|president of the Congress of the Union]] and a prominent figure for the Mexican left.<ref>{{Cite web |last=García |first=Diana |title=¿Qué significa la Banda Presidencial? Simbolismo de la toma de protesta de Sheinbaum |url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/mexico/2024/10/01/quien-le-entregara-la-banda-presidencial-a-claudia-sheinbaum/75465038007/ |access-date=1 October 2024 |website=The Arizona Republic |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Ledezma |first=Aram |date=1 October 2024 |title=¿Quién es Ifigenia Martinez, pionera de la izquierda y encargada de poner la Banda Presidencial a Claudia Sheinbaum? |url=https://mexico.as.com/actualidad/quien-es-ifigenia-martinez-pionera-de-la-izquierda-y-encargada-de-poner-la-banda-presidencial-a-claudia-sheinbaum-n/ |access-date=1 October 2024 |website=Diario AS |language=es-mx}}</ref> In her address to Congress, Sheinbaum thanked her predecessor, highlighted her historic election as the first woman to the presidency, pledged responsible fiscal policies, and reassured foreign investors.<ref>{{Cite web |author1=Elia Castillo Jiménez |author2=Zedryk Raziel |date=1 October 2024 |title=Sheinbaum, en su primer discurso como presidenta: "No les voy a defraudar" |url=https://elpais.com/mexico/2024-10-01/sheinbaum-en-su-primer-discurso-como-presidenta-no-les-voy-a-defraudar.html |access-date=1 October 2024 |website=El País México |language=es-MX}}</ref>

Her inauguration was attended by 105 representatives from various countries, including 16 heads of state and 23 delegates from international organizations.<ref>{{Cite web |date=1 October 2024 |title=Toma de protesta de Claudia Sheinbaum: Estos son los países y líderes que NO vendrán |url=https://mvsnoticias.com/nacional/2024/10/1/toma-de-protesta-de-claudia-sheinbaum-estos-son-los-paises-lideres-que-no-vendran-658972.html |access-date=1 October 2024 |website=MVS Noticias |language=es}}</ref> Notable attendees included Brazilian president [[Lula da Silva]], Chilean president [[Gabriel Boric]], Colombian president [[Gustavo Petro]], former German president [[Christian Wulff]], and US first lady [[Jill Biden]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Alonso |first=Ana |date=30 September 2024 |title=Claudia Sheinbaum, atada al legado de AMLO: un México más violento, menos democrático pero menos pobre |url=https://www.elindependiente.com/internacional/2024/10/01/claudia-sheinbaum-atada-al-legado-de-amlo-un-mexico-mas-violento-menos-democratico-pero-menos-pobre/ |access-date=1 October 2024 |website=El Independiente |language=es}}</ref> King [[Felipe VI]] of Spain was controversially not invited, with Sheinbaum citing his failure to respond to López Obrador's 2019 letter requesting an apology for the abuses committed during the [[Spanish conquest of the Aztec Empire|Spanish conquest]].<ref>{{Cite tweet |number=1839385334951653489 |user=Claudiashein |title=Comparto de nuevo el posicionamiento con dos precisiones que se fueron en la transcripción. |first=Claudia |last=Sheinbaum Pardo |date=26 September 2024 |access-date=1 October 2024 |language=Spanish |trans-title=I share my position once again with two clarifications on the transcription.}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=11 January 2021 |title=La carta íntegra en la que AMLO pidió al rey de España disculparse por los abusos de la Conquista |trans-title=Full letter in which AMLO asked the King of Spain to apologize for the abuses of the Conquest |url=https://www.infobae.com/america/mexico/2021/01/11/la-carta-integra-en-la-que-amlo-pidio-a-espana-disculparse-por-los-abusos-de-la-conquista/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230605053505/https://www.infobae.com/america/mexico/2021/01/11/la-carta-integra-en-la-que-amlo-pidio-a-espana-disculparse-por-los-abusos-de-la-conquista/ |archive-date=5 June 2023 |access-date=1 October 2024 |website=infobae |language=Spanish}}</ref> This prompted a boycott by the Spanish government.<ref>{{Cite web |date=26 September 2024 |title=Mexico excludes Spanish king from president's swearing-in |url=https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20240925-mexico-excludes-spanish-king-from-president-s-swearing-in |access-date=26 September 2024 |website=France 24 |agency=AFP}}</ref>

=== Cabinet ===
{{Main|Cabinet of Claudia Sheinbaum}}

Sheinbaum's initial cabinet was described as a mix of political allies and appointees with academic or specialized professional backgrounds.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=García |first1=Ana Karen |last2=Sosa Santiago |first2=María Fernanda |last3=Rojas |first3=Arturo |date=20 June 2024 |title=Sheinbaum anuncia a 6 integrantes de su gabinete; Ebrard va a la Secretaría de Economía |url=https://www.eleconomista.com.mx/politica/Sheinbaum-anuncia-a-6-integrantes-de-su-gabinete-Ebrard-va-a-la-Secretaria-de-Economia-20240620-0052.html |access-date=22 June 2025 |website=El Economista |language=es}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Núñez Albarrán |first=Ernesto |date=21 July 2024 |title=El gabinete de Sheinbaum: continuidad ¿con cambio? |url=https://animalpolitico.com/analisis/autores/explicador-politico/el-gabinete-de-sheinbaum-continuidad-con-cambio |access-date=22 June 2025 |website=Animal Politico |language=es}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web |last=Rodríguez |first=Esteban David |date=13 August 2024 |title=Gabinete de Sheinbaum: mezcla de continuidad, experiencia y lealtad |url=https://www.milenio.com/politica/gabinete-de-sheinbaum-mezcla-de-continuidad-experiencia-y-lealtad |access-date=22 June 2025 |website=Grupo Milenio |language=es}}</ref> Several figures from López Obrador's administration remained in office, including [[Rogelio Ramírez de la O]] as [[Secretary of Finance (Mexico)|Secretary of Finance]] and [[Ariadna Montiel Reyes]] as [[Secretariat of Welfare|Secretary of Welfare]].<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":3">{{Cite web |last=Zissis |first=Carin |last2=Harrison |first2=Chase |date=11 July 2024 |title=Who's Who in Claudia Sheinbaum's Cabinet |url=https://www.as-coa.org/articles/whos-who-claudia-sheinbaums-cabinet |access-date=13 November 2025 |website=AS/COA |language=en}}</ref> [[Rosa Icela Rodríguez]] was named [[Secretary of the Interior (Mexico)|Secretary of the Interior]], having previously served as López Obrador's [[Secretary of Security and Civilian Protection]] and as Sheinbaum's government secretary in Mexico City.<ref name=":3" /> Mario Delgado, who served as Morena's president from 2020 to 2024 and as general coordinator of Sheinbaum's presidential campaign, was appointed [[Secretary of Education (Mexico)|Secretary of Education]].<ref name=":3" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Herrera |first=Olivia Vázquez |date=7 July 2024 |title=CNTE estalla contra nombramiento de Mario Delgado en la SEP: "Fuera, impulsor de la Reforma Educativa" |url=https://www.infobae.com/mexico/2024/07/07/cnte-estalla-contra-nombramiento-de-mario-delgado-en-la-sep-fuera-impulsor-de-la-reforma-educativa/ |access-date=22 June 2025 |website=infobae |language=es}}</ref> From her Mexico City government, she appointed García Harfuch as Secretary of Security and Civilian Protection and [[Luz Elena González Escobar|Luz Elena González]] as [[Secretary of Energy (Mexico)|Secretary of Energy]].<ref name=":3" /> She also appointed her former presidential rival, Ebrard, as [[Secretariat of Economy|Secretary of Economy]], a move seen by analysts and business groups as conciliatory toward Morena’s moderate, pro-business wing and as strengthening Mexico’s position ahead of the upcoming [[United States–Mexico–Canada Agreement]] (USMCA) review.<ref>{{Cite web |date=21 June 2024 |title=Marcelo Ebrard, de jefe de Gobierno a secretario de Economía con Sheinbaum: ¿Qué cargos ha ocupado? |url=https://www.elfinanciero.com.mx/nacional/2024/06/21/marcelo-ebrard-secretaria-de-economia-gabinete-de-claudia-sheinbaum-que-cargos-ha-tenido-jefe-de-gobierno-canciller/ |access-date=22 June 2025 |website=El Financiero |language=es}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last1=Esposito |first1=Anthony |last2=Madry |first2=Kylie |date=20 June 2024 |title=Mexico president-elect taps Ebrard for economy chief, peso rallies |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/mexico-president-elect-names-initial-cabinet-members-2024-06-20/ |access-date=22 June 2025 |work=Reuters |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Monteiro |first=Thomas |date=24 July 2024 |title=Markets Approve Of Mexico’s New Economic Minister |url=https://gfmag.com/economics-policy-regulation/marcelo-ebrard-mexico-economy-minister/ |access-date=13 November 2025 |website=Global Finance Magazine |language=en-US}}</ref>

Sheinbaum expanded the federal cabinet by creating three new secretariats: the Secretariat of Women (replacing the {{Ill|National Institute for Women (Mexico)|lt=National Institute for Women|es|Instituto Nacional de las Mujeres (México)}}), the Secretariat of Science, Humanities, Technology and Innovation (replacing [[Consejo Nacional de Humanidades, Ciencias y Tecnologías|CONAHCYT]]), and the Digital Transformation and Telecommunications Agency.<ref name=":8">{{Cite web |title=Publican en el DOF reforma de Sheinbaum que crea tres Secretarías y una Agencia Digital |url=https://oem.com.mx/elsoldemexico/mexico/publican-en-el-dof-reforma-de-sheinbaum-que-crea-tres-secretarias-y-una-agencia-digital-18399215 |access-date=8 January 2025 |work=El Sol de México |language=es}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |author=Andrés García S |date=27 November 2024 |title=Estas serán las funciones de las secretarías de Mujeres y Ciencias; su creación ya fue aprobada por el Senado |url=https://www.infobae.com/mexico/2024/11/27/estas-seran-las-funciones-de-las-secretarias-de-mujeres-y-ciencias-su-creacion-ya-fue-aprobada-por-el-senado/ |access-date=8 January 2025 |website=infobae |language=es}}</ref> She also replaced the Secretariat of the Civil Service with the [[Secretariat of Anticorruption and Good Governance]].<ref name=":8" />

=== Domestic policy ===
Sheinbaum continued her predecessor's practice of holding "{{lang|es|mañaneras}}", regular press briefings in the morning.<ref>{{Cite web |date=3 October 2024 |title=Mexico's Sheinbaum keeps doing morning briefings, though her style is unlike her predecessor's |url=https://apnews.com/article/sheinbaum-mananera-lopez-obrador-mexico-president-472598f0eb3ab5a5003b3499fa47af4b |access-date=3 October 2024 |website=Associated Press |language=en}}</ref>

On 2 October 2024, the anniversary of the [[Tlatelolco massacre]], Sheinbaum issued a decree acknowledging the State's responsibility for the killings.<ref>{{Cite web |last=McDonnell |first=Patrick J. |date=2 October 2024 |title=Sheinbaum, a 'child of 1968,' apologizes for historic 'atrocity' in Tlatelolco, Mexico City |url=https://www.latimes.com/world-nation/story/2024-10-02/child-of-1968-sheinbaum-apologizes-for-1968-atrocity-in-tlatelolco-mexico-city |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241002221135/https://www.latimes.com/world-nation/story/2024-10-02/child-of-1968-sheinbaum-apologizes-for-1968-atrocity-in-tlatelolco-mexico-city |archive-date=2 October 2024 |access-date=25 October 2024 |website=Los Angeles Times |language=en}}</ref> The decree included a public apology, which was delivered by Secretary of the Interior Rosa Icela Rodríguez.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=México |first1=El Heraldo de |date=3 October 2024 |title=Mexico's Government apologizes for the 1968 Tlatelolco massacre |url=https://www.heraldousa.com/mexico/2024/10/03/mexicos-government-apologizes-for-the-1968-tlatelolco-massacre/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241003190154/https://www.heraldousa.com/mexico/2024/10/03/mexicos-government-apologizes-for-the-1968-tlatelolco-massacre/ |archive-date=3 October 2024 |access-date=25 October 2024 |website=Heraldo USA}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2 October 2024 |title=Claudia inicia su mandato recordando la represión de Estado y con disculpa a víctimas |url=https://www.sinembargo.mx/02-10-2024/4558037 |access-date=2 October 2024 |website=SinEmbargo MX |language=es}}</ref> [[File:La presidenta encabeza el Grito de Independencia 2025.jpg|thumb|Sheinbaum at the 2025 [[Cry of Dolores]] at the National Palace, Mexico City, marking the first time the ceremony was led by a woman.]]Faced with what many described as a looming constitutional crisis,<ref>{{Cite news |last=Graham |first=Thomas |date=4 November 2024 |title=Mexico president lashes out at supreme court amid looming constitutional crisis |url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2024/nov/04/mexico-supreme-court-claudia-sheinbaum-judicial-reform |access-date=29 June 2025 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last1=Romero |first1=Simon |last2=Villegas |first2=Paulina |date=2 November 2024 |title=A Way Out of Mexico's Constitutional Crisis? One Idea for Compromise Emerges. |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2024/11/02/world/americas/mexico-supreme-court-judicial-overhaul.html |access-date=29 June 2025 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref> Sheinbaum rejected a Supreme Court proposal to strike down parts of the judicial reform bill passed by López Obrador, asserting that the judiciary has no authority to review constitutional amendments and signaling she would not comply with any adverse ruling.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Kitroeff |first1=Natalie |last2=Rodríguez Mega |first2=Emiliano |date=1 November 2024 |title=Mexico's New President Faces Her First Major Crisis |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2024/11/01/world/americas/mexico-claudia-sheinbaum-judicial-overhaul.html |access-date=1 November 2024 |website=The New York Times}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=31 October 2024 |title=Mexico supreme court judges resign over reforms to allow voters to elect judiciary |url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2024/oct/31/mexico-supreme-court-judges-resign-voting-reforms |access-date=1 November 2024 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077 |agency=Agence France-Presse}}</ref> She subsequently published a bill enshrining constitutional supremacy, which limited legal challenges to constitutional amendments strictly to procedural grounds.<ref>{{Cite web |date=1 November 2024 |title=Supremacía constitucional entra en vigor: DOF publica reforma que 'blinda' cambios constitucionales |url=https://www.elfinanciero.com.mx/nacional/2024/11/01/supremacia-constitucional-entra-en-vigor-publica-dof-reforma-que-blinda-cambios-constitucionales/ |access-date=1 November 2024 |website=El Financiero |language=es}}</ref>

==== Crime and the drug war ====
Sheinbaum’s security strategy is built around four core pillars: addressing the root causes of violence, strengthening the National Guard, enhancing intelligence and investigative capabilities, and maintaining constant communication between the security cabinet and the country's [[List of states of Mexico|federative entities]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=8 October 2024 |title=Sheinbaum y Harfuch presentan nueva estrategia de Seguridad: ¿Cómo combatirán al crimen? |url=https://www.elfinanciero.com.mx/nacional/2024/10/08/nueva-estrategia-de-seguridad-de-claudia-sheinbaum-que-acciones-incluye/ |access-date=2 July 2025 |website=El Financiero |language=es}}</ref> She appointed [[Omar García Harfuch]] to head the [[Secretariat of Security and Civilian Protection]] (SSCP), a role he previously held in her Mexico City cabinet.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Barrera |first=Adriana |date=4 July 2024 |title=Mexico's Sheinbaum taps Garcia Harfuch as security minister in bid to tackle crime |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/mexicos-sheinbaum-names-harfuch-security-minister-2024-07-04/ |access-date=19 November 2024 |website=Reuters}}</ref> Her administration adopted a more hard-handed approach toward organized crime, with the SSCP going after organized crime's logistical networks and "violence generators",<ref>{{Cite web |last=Coste |first=Jacques |title=The Missing Elements in Sheinbaum's Crime-Fighting Strategy |url=https://www.americasquarterly.org/article/the-missing-elements-in-sheinbaums-crime-fighting-strategy/ |access-date=4 May 2025 |website=Americas Quarterly |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=16 January 2025 |title=Balance de Seguridad a 100 días de la Era Sheinbaum |url=https://www.mexicoevalua.org/balance-de-seguridad-a-100-dias-de-la-era-sheinbaum/ |access-date=4 May 2025 |website=México Evalúa |language=es}}</ref> marking a departure from López Obrador's "[[Abrazos, no balazos|hugs, not bullets]]" strategy.<ref name="AP News-2024b">{{Cite web |date=7 November 2024 |title=Mexico appears to abandon its 'hugs, not bullets' strategy as bloodshed plagues the country |url=https://apnews.com/article/mexico-drug-cartels-migrants-hugs-not-bullets-violence-5cf8bbefe68ea9762a0bdd23868029f3 |access-date=19 November 2024 |website=AP News |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=7 November 2024 |title=Bodies of 11 people, including 2 children, found on highway in Mexico weeks after city's mayor decapitated – CBS News |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/bodies-found-dumped-highway-guerrero-mexico/ |access-date=19 November 2024 |website=www.cbsnews.com |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=24 October 2024 |title=¿Adiós abrazos, hola balazos? Sheinbaum mostraría mano dura a cárteles tras violencia en Sinaloa, según NYT |url=https://www.elfinanciero.com.mx/nacional/2024/10/23/adios-abrazos-hola-balazos-sheinbaum-mostraria-mano-dura-a-carteles-tras-violencia-en-sinaloa-segun-nyt/ |access-date=19 November 2024 |website=El Financiero |language=es}}</ref> The SSPC's powers were expanded through legislation that facilitated closer collaboration with the [[Attorney General of Mexico|Attorney General's Office]], improved intelligence-gathering across all levels of government, and allowed the SSPC to request information from any agency for criminal investigations.<ref>{{Cite web |date=13 November 2024 |title=Senado avala "súper Secretaría de Seguridad"; turnan a San Lázaro reforma para darle más poder a García Harfuch |url=https://animalpolitico.com/politica/senado-aprueba-supersecretaria-garcia-harfuch |access-date=19 November 2024 |website=Animal Politico |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=31 December 2024 |title=Supersecretaría de Seguridad se estrena el 1 de enero; publican reforma constitucional |trans-title=Supersecretariat of Security premieres on January 1; constitutional reform published |url=https://www.eleconomista.com.mx/politica/supersecretaria-seguridad-estrenara-1-enero-publican-reforma-constitucional-20241231-740211.html |access-date=24 January 2025 |website=El Economista}}</ref> Her administration expanded the catalogue of crimes subject to mandatory [[pre-trial detention]], including [[extortion]], [[contraband]], the use of false tax receipts, and activities related to the production, trafficking, and distribution of synthetic drugs such as [[fentanyl]] and its derivatives.<ref>{{Cite web |date=31 December 2024 |title=Claudia Sheinbaum publica en el DOF la reforma sobre prisión preventiva oficiosa |url=https://www.eleconomista.com.mx/politica/claudia-sheinbaum-publica-dof-reforma-sobre-prision-preventiva-oficiosa-20241231-740216.html |access-date=17 December 2025 |website=El Economista |language=es}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=31 December 2024 |title=Publica el DOF la Prisión Preventiva para Extorsión y Fentanilo |url=https://www.nmas.com.mx/nacional/publica-el-dof-la-prision-preventiva-para-extorsion-y-fentanilo/ |access-date=17 December 2025 |website=N+ |language=es-MX}}</ref> She also continued the militarization of the National Guard, endorsing its continued integration into the Secretariat of National Defense, and launched a nationwide [[gun buyback program]] called {{lang|es|Sí al Desarme, Sí a la Paz}} ({{Literal translation|Yes to Disarmament, Yes to Peace}}) to reduce the number of weapons in circulation.<ref>{{Cite web |date=13 January 2025 |title=Mexico offers cash to get guns off the streets: $1,200 for an AK-47 rifle and $1,300 for a machine gun |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/mexico-cash-for-guns-campaign-ak-47-machine-gun/ |access-date=3 February 2025 |website=CBS News |language=en-US}}</ref>

During the first months of Sheinbaum's administration, the homicide rate decreased by approximately 25%, with daily homicides falling from 86.9 at the start of her term to 64.5 as of May 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ortega |first=Eduardo |date=11 June 2025 |title=Gobierno federal resalta baja de 25.8% en homicidios en los últimos 8 meses |url=https://www.elfinanciero.com.mx/nacional/2025/06/11/gobierno-federal-resalta-baja-de-258-en-homicidios-en-los-ultimos-8-meses/ |access-date=26 June 2025 |website=El Financiero |language=es}}</ref> Other high-impact crimes, including kidnappings and bank robberies, also decreased during this period, although incidents of extortion and the number of disappearances have continued to rise,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Contreras |first=Jorge |date=16 May 2025 |title=Banamex ve disminución sostenida de violencia en gobierno de Sheinbaum |url=https://www.infobae.com/mexico/2025/05/16/banamex-ve-disminucion-sostenida-de-violencia-en-gobierno-de-sheinbaum/ |access-date=26 June 2025 |website=infobae |language=es}}</ref> with about 8,000 new cases of [[Missing persons in Mexico|disappeared persons]] reported during the same period.<ref>{{cite web |last=Lopez |first=Oscar |date=4 May 2025 |title=Mexico's president has notched some big wins, but she has a lot of work ahead |url=https://www.latimes.com/opinion/story/2025-05-04/claudia-sheinbaum-mexico-president-trump-trade-violence-crime |access-date=5 July 2025 |newspaper=Los Angeles Times}}</ref> The administration reported significant increases in drug seizures; by June 2025, authorities had confiscated approximately 178 tonnes of narcotics, including 3 million fentanyl pills, from 1,150 clandestine laboratories.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Estrada |first=Aranza |date=24 June 2025 |title=Harfuch presenta avances en estrategia de seguridad; destaca más de mil detenciones y decomiso de 178 toneladas de droga |url=https://www.infobae.com/mexico/2025/06/24/harfuch-presenta-avances-en-estrategia-de-seguridad-destaca-mas-de-mil-detenciones-y-decomiso-de-178-toneladas-de-droga/ |access-date=26 June 2025 |website=infobae |language=es-ES}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=24 June 2025 |title=Caen 22 objetivos prioritarios en 15 días; anuncia Omar García Harfuch |url=https://abcnoticias.mx/nacional/2025/6/24/caen-22-objetivos-prioritarios-en-15-dias-anuncia-omar-garcia-harfuch-252790.html |access-date=26 June 2025 |website=ABC Noticias |language=es}}</ref> Efforts to combat fuel theft, known as ''[[Huachicolero|huachicol]]'', were also expanded, with multiple seizures conducted at sea and at illegal refineries across the country.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Chinea |first=Eyanir |date=23 June 2025 |title=Sheinbaum endurece la lucha contra el huachicol |url=https://elpais.com/mexico/2025-06-23/sheinbaum-endurece-la-lucha-contra-el-huachicol-fiscal.html |access-date=26 June 2025 |website=El País México |language=es}}</ref>

Despite reported gains, Sheinbaum's presidency has been marked by ongoing cartel violence. Across the country, [[List of politicians killed during the presidency of Claudia Sheinbaum|political assassinations]] have continued at a high pace, leaving local officials particularly vulnerable.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ramírez |first=Rafael |date=27 July 2025 |title=Aumenta violencia política en la primera mitad de 2025: Integralia registra 112 asesinatos en 253 incidentes |url=https://oem.com.mx/elsoldemexico/mexico/escala-la-violencia-politica-en-mexico-durante-el-primer-semestre-de-2025-integralia-registra-112-asesinatos-en-253-inc-24960847 |access-date=13 December 2025 |website=El Sol de Mexico |language=es}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=E. Martínez |first=Carlos |date=3 November 2025 |title=Registran 56 asesinatos de actores políticos en lo que va de 2025; siete son alcaldes, entre ellos Carlos Manzo |url=https://animalpolitico.com/seguridad/registran-56-asesinatos-actores-politicos-2025-alcaldes-carlos-manzo |access-date=13 December 2025 |website=Animal Politico |language=es}}</ref> [[Infighting in the Sinaloa Cartel|Clashes between rival factions of the Sinaloa Cartel]] contributed to a more than 400% increase in homicides in [[Sinaloa]] during the first half of 2025, prompting federal deployment of additional forces and arrests of mid-to-high ranking members of both factions.<ref>{{Cite web |date=30 September 2024 |title=Anuncian operativo contra narcoguerra en Sinaloa |url=https://plazadearmas.com.mx/anuncian-operativo-contra-narcoguerra-en-sinaloa/ |access-date=24 October 2024 |website=Plaza de Armas: Querétaro |language=es}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last1=Muñoz-Ledo |first1=Rocío |last2=Schmitz |first2=Avery |last3=Calderon |first3=Veronica |date=18 August 2025 |title=A cartel war bleeding Sinaloa dry: homicides rise 400% in the year after the fall of 'El Mayo' |url=https://www.cnn.com/2025/08/18/americas/mexico-killings-sinaloa-cartel-kingpin-latam-intl |access-date=27 September 2025 |website=CNN |language=en}}</ref> In March 2025, authorities discovered a [[Jalisco extermination camp|training camp in Teuchitlán, Jalisco]], allegedly used by the Jalisco New Generation Cartel (CJNG) as a forced recruitment center, which resulted in the arrest of a dozen people, including the municipality's mayor and alleged CJNG recruiter "El Comandante Lastra".<ref>{{Cite web |date=4 May 2025 |title=Mexican mayor arrested in connection to alleged drug cartel training camp, official says – CBS News |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/mexico-mayor-arrested-drug-cartel-training-camp-jalisco-new-generation/ |access-date=27 September 2025 |website=www.cbsnews.com |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=4 May 2025 |title=Mexican mayor arrested in probe of alleged drug cartel ranch: govt source |url=https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20250504-mexican-mayor-arrested-in-probe-of-alleged-drug-cartel-ranch-govt-source |access-date=27 September 2025 |website=France 24 |language=en}}</ref> Violence in [[Michoacán]] also intensified, defined by a turf war between the CJNG and [[Cárteles Unidos]] that has led to rampant extortion of the state's avocado and lime industries and a wave of assassinations targeting public and community leaders, including the murder of [[Uruapan]]'s mayor, [[Carlos Manzo]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=3 November 2025 |title=Registran 56 asesinatos de actores políticos en lo que va de 2025; siete son alcaldes, entre ellos Carlos Manzo |url=https://animalpolitico.com/seguridad/registran-56-asesinatos-actores-politicos-2025-alcaldes-carlos-manzo |access-date=9 November 2025 |website=Animal Politico |language=es}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=4 November 2025 |title=Michoacán: Tierra de cárteles |url=https://codigomagenta.com.mx/michoacan-tierra-de-carteles/ |access-date=9 November 2025 |website=Código Magenta |language=es}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2 November 2025 |title=Violencia ‘se desata’ en Michoacán: ¿Qué cárteles operan en el estado y quienes pelean ‘Tierra Caliente’? |url=https://www.elfinanciero.com.mx/estados/2025/11/02/que-carteles-operan-en-michoacan-violencia-en-tierra-caliente-crimen-organizado-en-uruapan-asesinato-de-carlos-manzo/ |access-date=9 November 2025 |website=El Financiero |language=es}}</ref>

==== Energy ====
Sheinbaum continued elements of the energy nationalism advanced by Andrés Manuel López Obrador, aiming to strengthen the state-owned [[Federal Electricity Commission]] (CFE) and [[Petróleos Mexicanos]] (Pemex).<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Quiroz |first1=Alberto |last2=Ramírez Fuentes |first2=Carlos |date=4 November 2024 |title=Mexico's Risky New Energy Reform |url=https://www.americasquarterly.org/article/mexicos-risky-new-energy-reform/ |access-date=11 May 2025 |website=Americas Quarterly |language=en-US}}</ref> On 30 October 2024, she published a constitutional amendment that reclassified both entities as public institutions and established a mandate for the CFE to retain 54% of the national electricity generation market, with the remaining 46% allocated to private producers.<ref>{{Cite web |date=31 October 2024 |title=President Sheinbaum Restores PEMEX, CFE as Public Entities |url=https://mexicobusiness.news/energy/news/president-sheinbaum-restores-pemex-cfe-public-entities?tag=energy |access-date=31 October 2024 |website=Mexico Business |language=en}}</ref> Her administration also revised oil production targets, setting a goal of 1.8 million barrels per day—lower than the 2 million barrels pursued under López Obrador.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Nava |first=Diana |date=9 October 2024 |title=Sheinbaum marca distancia del sexenio anterior: Más energías limpias y menos petróleo |url=https://expansion.mx/empresas/2024/10/09/sheinbaum-marca-distancia-sexenio-anterior-mas-energias-limpias |access-date=11 May 2025 |website=Expansión |language=es}}</ref>

==== Infrastructure and passenger rail ====
During her presidency, Sheinbaum made the expansion of Mexico’s passenger rail network a central element of her infrastructure agenda, promoting state-led development of intercity rail and enacting a constitutional amendment restoring federal authority over passenger rail operations.<ref>{{Cite web |author1=Alonso Urrutia |author2=Alma E. Muñoz |date=30 October 2024 |title=Sheinbaum firma decreto que "devuelve Pemex y CFE al pueblo de México" |url=https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2024/10/30/politica/sheinbaum-firma-decreto-que-201cdevuelve-a-pemex-y-a-cfe-al-pueblo-de-mexico201d-1050 |access-date=31 October 2024 |website=La Jornada |language=es}}</ref> Her administration announced plans to construct approximately 3,000 kilometres of new lines, including the Mexico–Pachuca, Mexico–Nuevo Laredo, and Mexico–Nogales lines.<ref>{{Cite web |date=23 October 2024 |title=Mexico's president sets bold agenda to transform mobility and infrastructure |url=https://www.intertraffic.com/news/infrastructure/mexico-president-bold-agenda-transform-mobility-infrastructure |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241104123006/https://www.intertraffic.com/news/infrastructure/mexico-president-bold-agenda-transform-mobility-infrastructure |archive-date=4 November 2024 |access-date=25 October 2024 |website=www.intertraffic.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2 December 2024 |title=Mexico to Invest MX$157 Billion in Railway Projects |url=https://mexicobusiness.news/infrastructure/news/mexico-invest-mx157-billion-railway-projects-0 |access-date=16 December 2024 |website=Mexico Business |language=en}}</ref> She also oversaw the inauguration of the final sections of the [[Tren Maya]] in 2024,<ref>{{Cite web |date=15 December 2024 |title=All aboard! Entire 1,554 kilometers of Mexico's Maya Train circuit open for travel |url=https://riviera-maya-news.com/all-aboard-entire-1554-kilometers-of-mexicos-maya-train-circuit-open-for-travel/2024.html |access-date=16 December 2024 |website=Riviera Maya News |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=28 November 2024 |title=The Federal Government will invest 49 billion pesos for the Maya Cargo Train in Yucatan and Quintana Roo |url=https://www.theyucatantimes.com/2024/11/the-federal-government-will-invest-49-billion-pesos-for-the-maya-cargo-train-in-yucatan-and-quintana-roo/ |access-date=16 December 2024 |work=The Yucatan Times |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Vázquez Herrera |first=Olivia |date=15 December 2024 |title=Sheinbaum celebra 1er año del Tren Maya, inaugura tramos y recuerda: "la privatización fue uno de los errores más costosos" |url=https://www.infobae.com/mexico/2024/12/15/sheinbaum-celebra-1er-ano-del-tren-maya-inaugura-tramos-y-recuerda-la-privatizacion-fue-uno-de-los-errores-mas-costosos/ |access-date=16 December 2024 |website=infobae |language=es}}</ref> and in February 2026 she inaugurated the [[Santa Fe railway station (Mexico City)|Santa Fe]]–[[Observatorio railway station|Observatorio]] section of [[El Insurgente|Tren El Insurgente]], completing the Mexico City–Toluca interurban rail link begun in 2014.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Corona |first=Sonia |date=3 February 2026 |title=Obras por 12 años y 100.000 millones de pesos en inversión: México echa andar el tren que une la capital con Toluca |url=https://elpais.com/mexico/2026-02-03/obras-por-12-anos-y-100000-millones-de-pesos-en-inversion-mexico-echa-andar-el-tren-interurbano-mexico-toluca.html |access-date=7 February 2026 |website=El País México |language=es}}</ref>

In 2024, Sheinbaum announced a MX$33 billion investment to modernize six ports across Mexico: [[Ensenada, Baja California]]; [[Manzanillo, Colima]]; [[Lázaro Cárdenas, Michoacán]]; [[Acapulco, Guerrero]]; [[Veracruz, Veracruz]]; and Progreso, Yucatán.<ref>{{Cite web |date=6 December 2024 |title=Mexico announces US $1.6B investment to modernize 6 major maritime ports |url=https://mexiconewsdaily.com/business/mexico-modernize-6-maritime-ports/ |access-date=16 December 2024 |website=Mexico News Daily |language=en-US}}</ref>

Sheinbaum has continued her predecessor's practice of employing [[SEDENA]]'s Military Engineers Corps. to build government infrastructure projects.<ref name="mexpca:train">{{Cite web |date=10 October 2024 |title=Sheinbaum Kicks off construction of AIFA-Pachuca Passenger Train |url=https://mexicobusiness.news/infrastructure/news/sheinbaum-kicks-construction-aifa-pachuca-passenger-train |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260312165636/https://mexicobusiness.news/infrastructure/news/sheinbaum-kicks-construction-aifa-pachuca-passenger-train |archive-date=12 March 2026 |access-date=25 October 2024 |website=Mexico Business News}}</ref>

==== Institutional reform ====
Sheinbaum continued the centralization of executive authority by dissolving seven autonomous agencies in late 2024: the [[Federal Telecommunications Institute]] (IFT), the [[Comisión Federal de Competencia Económica|Federal Economic Competition Commission]] (COFECE), the [[National Institute of Transparency for Access to Information and Personal Data Protection|National Institute for Transparency]] (INAI), the Energy Regulatory Commission (CRE), the National Hydrocarbons Commission (CNH), the [[National Council for the Evaluation of Social Development Policy]] (CONEVAL), and the National Institute for the Evaluation of Education (MejorEdu).<ref>{{Cite web |last=Marsan |first=Eduardo |date=24 December 2024 |title=Desaparición de los organismos autónomos; comenzó con AMLO y culminó con Sheinbaum |url=https://www.infobae.com/mexico/2024/12/24/desaparicion-de-los-organismos-autonomos-comenzo-con-amlo-y-culmino-con-sheinbaum/ |access-date=8 January 2025 |website=infobae |language=es}}</ref> Their functions were transferred to various cabinet ministries in what the administration described as an effort to streamline government operations and reduce public spending, though critics argued that the measure undermined transparency, regulatory independence, and checks on executive power.<ref>{{Cite web |date=29 November 2024 |title=As Mexico advances plan to dissolve watchdog agencies, critics cry foul |url=https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/11/29/as-mexico-advances-plan-to-dissolve-watchdog-agencies-critics-cry-foul |access-date=5 October 2025 |website=Al Jazeera |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Statement Regarding the Elimination of Independent Agencies in Mexico |url=https://www.nycbar.org/reports/statement-regarding-the-elimination-of-independent-agencies-in-mexico/ |access-date=5 October 2025 |website=New York City Bar Association |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Oré |first=Diego |date=21 November 2024 |title=Mexico's lower house votes to abolish autonomous bodies |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/mexicos-lower-house-votes-abolish-autonomous-bodies-2024-11-21/ |access-date=5 October 2025 |work=Reuters |language=en}}</ref>

On 1 April 2025, Sheinbaum published a constitutional reform to prohibit immediate reelection and bar close relatives of incumbents from running for the same office; although initially set for 2027, its implementation was postponed to 2030 following negotiations within the ruling coalition in the Senate.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Escobar |first=Dalila |date=5 February 2025 |title=Sheinbaum anunció dos reformas constitucionales: no reelección y contra el nepotismo |url=https://www.proceso.com.mx/nacional/2025/2/5/sheinbaum-anuncio-dos-reformas-constitucionales-no-reeleccion-contra-el-nepotismo-345033.html |access-date=22 June 2025 |website=Proceso |language=es}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Rojas |first=Arturo |date=26 February 2025 |title=Sheinbaum respalda aplicación en 2030 de la reforma contra el nepotismo |url=https://www.eleconomista.com.mx/politica/sheinbaum-respalda-aplicacion-2030-reforma-nepotismo-20250226-748040.html |access-date=22 June 2025 |website=El Economista |language=es}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last1=Jornada |first1=La |last2=Redacción |first2=La |date=1 April 2025 |title=Publican en DOF decretos sobre soberanía, nepotismo electoral y no relección |url=https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2025/04/01/politica/publica-dof-decretos-sobre-soberania-nacional-nepotismo-electoral-y-no-releccion |access-date=22 June 2025 |website=La Jornada |language=es}}</ref> In February 2026, Sheinbaum proposed a broader electoral reform package to reduce the size of the [[Senate of the Republic (Mexico)|Senate]], modify proportional representation, cut party financing and electoral costs, eliminate the preliminary results program (PREP), and regulate the use of artificial intelligence in campaigns;<ref>{{Cite web |last=Morland |first=Sarah |last2=Pelaez-fernandez |first2=Aida |date=2026-02-25 |title=Mexico's Sheinbaum presents electoral reform that aims to slash spending by 25% |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/mexicos-sheinbaum-presents-electoral-reform-bill-2026-02-25/ |access-date=2026-03-23 |website=Reuters}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-02-25 |title=Morena's electoral reform would shrink the Senate, cut election budget and simplify voting from abroad |url=https://mexiconewsdaily.com/news/morenas-proposed-electoral-reform-would-shrink-the-senatea/ |access-date=2026-03-24 |website=Mexico News Daily |language=en}}</ref> however, the proposal failed to obtain a two-thirds majority after coalition allies—the [[Ecologist Green Party of Mexico]] (PVEM) and the [[Labor Party (Mexico)|Labor Party]] (PT)—withheld support amid concerns that the changes would weaken smaller parties, reduce their political influence, and concentrate power in the ruling party.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Oré |first=Diego |last2=Cortes |first2=Raul |date=2026-03-11 |title=Mexico's lower house rejects Sheinbaum's electoral reform, 'Plan B' looms |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/mexicos-lower-house-rejects-president-sheinbaums-electoral-reform-2026-03-11/ |access-date=2026-03-23 |website=Reuters}}</ref>

==== Protests and social unrest ====
The [[Coordinadora Nacional de Trabajadores de la Educación]] (CNTE) organized repeated strikes, work stoppages, and protest encampments, pressuring the government to fulfill campaign promises regarding the repeal of the 2007 ISSSTE Law and the improvement of pension benefits.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Poy |first=Laura |last2=Laureles |first2=Jared |date=7 March 2025 |title=Marcha CNTE rumbo al Zócalo contra la iniciativa presidencial a ley del Issste |url=https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2025/03/07/sociedad/marcha-cnte-rumbo-al-zocalo-en-demanda-de-abrogacion-de-ley-del-issste-de-2007 |access-date=13 December 2025 |website=La Jornada |language=es}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=16 May 2025 |title=Marcha la CNTE y toma el Zócalo |url=https://www.jornada.com.mx/2025/05/16/politica/007n2pol |access-date=13 December 2025 |website=La Jornada |language=es}}</ref> In the fall of 2025, widespread farmer strikes and highway blockades erupted across multiple states, with agricultural workers and truckers demanding higher guaranteed crop prices, improved highway security, and the rejection of a water reform bill promoted by the government; these actions frequently paralyzed transport routes leading into Mexico City.<ref>{{Cite web |date=4 December 2025 |title=Farmers block Mexico's Congress with tractors in protest against new national water law proposal |url=https://apnews.com/article/mexico-farmers-protest-water-law-a0e4d9f51e4e6d672a9240f4c5237aa8 |access-date=13 December 2025 |website=AP News |language=en}}</ref> In November 2025, a [[2025 Mexican protests|series of demonstrations]] opposing the administration—sparked in part by the assassination of Uruapan mayor Carlos Manzo—took place in several cities; Sheinbaum characterized the protests as politically motivated and lacking organic support.<ref>{{Cite web |date=16 November 2025 |title=Gen Z-styled protests spread in Mexico, fueled by mayor's murder |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/gen-z-styled-protests-spread-mexico-fueled-by-mayors-murder-2025-11-16/ |website=Reuters}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Ventura |first=Jorge |date=17 November 2025 |title=At least 120 hurt in Gen Z protests over corruption in Mexico |url=https://www.newsnationnow.com/world/gen-z-protests-corruption-mexico/}}</ref>

==== Welfare ====
Sheinbaum expanded federal social programs including the introduction of the Women's Wellbeing Pension (''Pensión Mujeres Bienestar''), which provides bimonthly financial assistance to senior women aged 60 to 64,<ref>{{Cite web |date=8 October 2024 |title=Pensión Mujeres Bienestar |trans-title=Women's Wellbeing Pension |url=https://programasparaelbienestar.gob.mx/pension-mujeres-bienestar/ |access-date=15 October 2024 |website=Gobierno de México, Programas para el Bienestar |language=es}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=8 October 2024 |title=Pensión del Bienestar para mujeres de 60 a 64 años: monto, requisitos, cuándo y cómo registrarse y más |trans-title=Wellbeing Pension for Women Aged 60 to 64: amount, requirements, when and how to apply and more |url=https://cnnespanol.cnn.com/2024/10/08/pension-del-bienestar-mujeres-60-64-anos-monto-requisitos-registro-fechas-orix |access-date=15 October 2024 |website=CNN |language=es}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Zúñiga |first=Alejandra |date=3 October 2024 |title=Pensión para el Bienestar de Mujeres Adultas Mayores: así puedes registrarte al programa si tienes 60 a 64 años |trans-title=Wellbeing Pension for Senior Women: this is how you can apply for the program if you are 60–64 years old |url=https://www.infobae.com/mexico/2024/10/03/pension-para-el-bienestar-de-mujeres-adultas-mayores-asi-puedes-registrarte-al-programa-si-tienes-60-a-64-anos/ |access-date=3 October 2024 |website=infobae |language=es}}</ref> and the launch of the House to House Health (''Salud Casa a Casa'') program, which delivers home-based medical care to elderly people and individuals with disabilities.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Zerega |first=Georgina |date=7 October 2024 |title=Atención médica casa por casa a 13,6 millones de personas: así es el ambicioso plan de salud de Sheinbaum |trans-title=House-to-house medical care for 13.6 million people: This is Sheinbaum's ambitious health plan. |url=https://elpais.com/mexico/2024-10-07/atencion-medica-casa-por-casa-a-136-millones-de-personas-asi-es-el-ambicioso-plan-de-salud-de-sheinbaum.html |access-date=15 January 2025 |website=El País México |language=es}}</ref> She also renamed the Benito Juárez Scholarship (''Beca Benito Juárez'') to the Rita Cetina Gutiérrez Universal Scholarship (''Beca Universal Rita Cetina Gutiérrez''), expanding it to provide bimonthly financial aid to all families with children enrolled in the public [[Education in Mexico#Structure of the basic education system|basic educational system]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Baena |first=Mayte |date=4 October 2024 |title=Beca Universal Rita Cetina Gutiérrez: anuncian pago de mil 900 pesos para estudiantes de primaria y secundaria |trans-title=Rita Cetina Gutiérrez Universal Scholarship: payment of 1,900 pesos announced for primary and secondary school students |url=https://www.infobae.com/mexico/2024/10/04/beca-universal-rita-cetina-gutierrez-anuncian-pago-de-mil-900-pesos-para-estudiante-de-educacion-basica/ |access-date=4 October 2024 |website=infobae |language=es}}</ref> On 2 December 2024, Sheinbaum elevated several social programs to constitutional law.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Flores |first=Claudia |date=2 December 2024 |title=Sheinbaum firma decreto para que Universidad Nacional Rosario Castellanos sea nacional y programas del Bienestar "un derecho" |trans-title=Sheinbaum signs a decree to make the Rosario Castellanos National University national and to establish Well-being programs as a "right." |url=https://www.infobae.com/mexico/2024/12/02/claudia-sheinbaum-anuncia-que-la-mayoria-de-los-programas-del-bienestar-hoy-se-publicaran-en-el-dof-ya-son-un-derecho/ |access-date=15 January 2025 |website=infobae |language=es}}</ref> Her administration has continued to prioritize social spending in budget allocations, with social program spending equivalent to approximately 3% of gross domestic product, according to the 2026 budget.<ref>{{Cite web |date=9 September 2025 |title=Pensión Bienestar: ¿Cuánto dinero recibirá el programa en el Presupuesto 2026? |url=https://www.elfinanciero.com.mx/economia/2025/09/08/aumento-programas-y-pension-bienestar-paquete-economico-2026-de-cuanto-es-la-inversion/ |access-date=21 December 2025 |website=El Financiero |language=es}}</ref>

Sheinbaum proposed a constitutional reform providing that annual minimum wage increases may not be set below the inflation rate; while the reform had not yet been enacted,<ref>{{Cite web |date=17 December 2024 |title=Morena “congela” la reforma para incrementar el salario mínimo por arriba de la inflación |url=https://animalpolitico.com/politica/reforma-salario-minimo-aumento-inflacion |access-date=21 December 2025 |website=Animal Politico |language=es}}</ref> wage policy has been implemented in line with this framework, with the daily minimum wage set at MX$278.80 and later increased to MX$315.04 for 2026, consistent with a stated objective of reaching the equivalent of 2.5 [[Market basket|food baskets]] by 2030.<ref>{{Cite web |date=14 September 2025 |title=Promete Sheinbaum que en 2030 el salario mínimo alcanzará a cubrir 2.5 canastas básicas |url=https://www.eleconomista.com.mx/capital-humano/promete-sheinbaum-2030-salario-minimo-alcanzara-cubrir-2-5-canastas-basicas-20250914-777184.html |access-date=21 December 2025 |website=El Economista |language=es}}</ref> The administration also formalized the ''[[Ley Silla]]'', granting service-sector workers the right to seating and rest periods,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hernández |first=Gerardo |date=17 June 2025 |title=¡Es oficial! Entra en vigor la Ley Silla y el derecho al descanso en la jornada laboral |url=https://www.eleconomista.com.mx/capital-humano/oficial-entra-vigor-ley-silla-derecho-descanso-jornada-laboral-20250617-763983.html |access-date=21 December 2025 |website=El Economista |language=es}}</ref> enacted a reform regulating digital platform work that extends [[Mexican Social Security Institute|IMSS]] social security coverage and mandatory occupational accident insurance to active platform workers,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Huitrón |first=Lorna |date=28 June 2025 |title=Nuevas reglas del IMSS para repartidores de plataformas digitales entran en vigor |url=https://www.infobae.com/mexico/2025/06/28/nuevas-reglas-del-imss-para-repartidores-de-plataformas-digitales-entran-en-vigor/ |access-date=21 December 2025 |website=infobae |language=es}}</ref> and reached a tripartite agreement to gradually reduce the legal workweek from 48 to 40 hours beginning in 2027.<ref>{{Cite web |date=3 December 2025 |title=Labor ministry unveils business-backed plan to reduce workweek to 40 hours |url=https://mexiconewsdaily.com/news/labor-ministry-workweek-48-40-hours/ |access-date=21 December 2025 |website=Mexico News Daily |language=en-US}}</ref>

=== Foreign policy ===
{{Main|Presidency of Claudia Sheinbaum#Foreign policy}}{{See also|List of international presidential trips made by Claudia Sheinbaum}}Sheinbaum's presidency has been dominated by relations with the [[United States]] under the [[Second presidency of Donald Trump|second administration]] of [[Donald Trump]]. After Trump threatened tariffs of 25% on Mexican goods in early 2025, she negotiated repeated pauses and secured exemptions for goods that complied with the [[United States–Mexico–Canada Agreement]].<ref name="npr-pause2">{{cite news |last=Neill |first=Tara |last2=Peralta |first2=Eyder |last3=Jacobs |first3=Emma |date=3 February 2025 |title=Trump puts Mexico and Canada tariffs on hold |url=https://www.npr.org/2025/02/03/nx-s1-5285334/mexico-us-canada-tariffs-trump-sheinbaum |access-date=19 June 2026 |work=[[NPR]]}}</ref><ref name="newsweek-tariffs">{{cite news |date=7 April 2025 |title=As the World Turns on Trump, Mexico's Claudia Sheinbaum Has Other Plans |url=https://www.newsweek.com/claudia-sheinbaum-mexico-donald-trump-tariffs-2055581 |access-date=19 June 2026 |work=[[Newsweek]]}}</ref> Her government condemned the United States designation of Mexican drug cartels as [[United States Department of State list of Foreign Terrorist Organizations|foreign terrorist organizations]],<ref name="npr-sovereignty">{{cite news |last=Peralta |first=Eyder |date=20 February 2025 |title=Mexico warns the US not to invade its sovereignty in fight against cartels |url=https://www.npr.org/2025/02/20/nx-s1-5304248/mexico-warns-the-us-not-to-invade-our-sovereignty-in-fight-against-cartels |access-date=19 June 2026 |work=[[NPR]]}}</ref> and she rejected Trump's offer to send United States troops into Mexico, saying that "sovereignty is not for sale".<ref name="hill-troops2">{{cite news |last=Fields |first=Ashleigh |date=3 May 2025 |title=Claudia Sheinbaum says she denied Donald Trump offer to target Mexican cartels with US troops |url=https://thehill.com/policy/international/5281418-mexico-trump-sheinbaum-troops-immigration-drugs/ |access-date=19 June 2026 |work=[[The Hill (newspaper)|The Hill]]}}</ref> At the same time, Mexico expanded cooperation, transferring dozens of imprisoned cartel figures to the United States<ref name="bbc-29">{{cite news |last=Mackintosh |first=Thomas |last2=Grant |first2=Will |date=28 February 2025 |title=Notorious Mexican drug lord among 29 extradited to US |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cx2995y25lyo |access-date=19 June 2026 |work=[[BBC News]]}}</ref> and sharing intelligence in operations against cartel leaders, including the killing of [[Jalisco New Generation Cartel|CJNG]] leader [[Nemesio Oseguera Cervantes|"El Mencho"]] in 2026.<ref name="fox-mencho">{{cite news |last=Chu |first=Bonny |last2=Mion |first2=Landon |date=23 February 2026 |title=Major drug lord 'El Mencho' killed in Mexican military operation with US intelligence support |url=https://www.foxnews.com/world/major-drug-lord-el-mencho-killed-mexican-military-operation-us-intelligence-support |access-date=19 June 2026 |work=[[Fox News]]}}</ref> Sheinbaum also opposed United States military action abroad as contrary to international law, objecting to a [[United States strikes on alleged drug traffickers during Operation Southern Spear|campaign of strikes on suspected drug-trafficking boats]] in international waters<ref name="mnd-boats">{{cite news |date=29 October 2025 |title=Sheinbaum condemns US boat strikes near Mexico's waters |url=https://mexiconewsdaily.com/politics/sheinbaum-condemns-us-boat-strikes-wednesdays-mananera-recapped/ |access-date=19 June 2026 |work=Mexico News Daily}}</ref> and condemned [[2026 United States intervention in Venezuela|a United States military operation in Venezuela]] in January 2026.<ref name="mnd-venezuela2">{{cite news |date=3 January 2026 |title=Sheinbaum condemns US military intervention in Venezuela |url=https://mexiconewsdaily.com/news/sheinbaum-condemns-us-military-intervention-in-venezuela-trump-says-somethings-going-to-have-to-be-done-with-mexico/ |access-date=19 June 2026 |work=Mexico News Daily}}</ref>

Sheinbaum has sought to deepen Mexico's engagement with Latin America, calling for greater regional economic integration at the 2025 [[Community of Latin American and Caribbean States|CELAC]] summit<ref name="mnd-celac">{{cite news |date=9 April 2025 |title=Sheinbaum turns her gaze toward Latin America at CELAC summit in Honduras |url=https://mexiconewsdaily.com/news/sheinbaum-turns-her-gaze-toward-latin-america-at-celac-summit-in-honduras/ |access-date=19 June 2026 |work=Mexico News Daily}}</ref> and aligning with other left-led governments.<ref name="democrata-gpm">{{cite news |date=18 April 2026 |title=Progressive summit in Barcelona: Sánchez gathers Lula, Petro and Sheinbaum to strengthen a progressive axis |url=https://www.democrata.es/en/politics/progressive-summit-in-barcelona-sanchez-lula-petro-and-sheinbaum-for-peace/ |access-date=19 June 2026 |work=Demócrata}}</ref> She has maintained close ties with [[Cuba]] through oil shipments and later humanitarian aid.<ref name="opis-cuba2">{{cite news |date=8 January 2026 |title=Sheinbaum Says Mexico Will Remain Key Fuel Supplier to Cuba As Venezuela Exports Decline |url=https://www.opis.com/resources/energy-market-news-from-opis/sheinbaum-says-mexico-will-remain-key-fuel-supplier-to-cuba-as-venezuela-exports-decline/ |access-date=19 June 2026 |work=OPIS}}</ref><ref name="pd-aid2">{{cite news |last=Meriguet |first=Pablo |date=10 February 2026 |title=Mexico sends shipment of humanitarian aid to Cuba |url=https://peoplesdispatch.org/2026/02/10/mexico-sends-shipment-of-humanitarian-aid-to-cuba/ |access-date=19 June 2026 |work=Peoples Dispatch}}</ref> Mexico's relations with [[Ecuador]] remained severed following the [[2024 raid on the Mexican embassy in Quito|2024 raid on its embassy in Quito]],<ref name="aol-ecuador2">{{cite news |date=16 April 2025 |title=Mexico's Sheinbaum says country will not renew diplomatic relations with Ecuador |url=https://www.usnews.com/news/world/articles/2025-04-16/mexicos-sheinbaum-says-country-will-not-renew-diplomatic-relations-with-ecuador |access-date=19 June 2026 |work=U.S. News & World Report |agency=Reuters}}</ref> and broke down with [[Peru]] in November 2025 after Mexico granted asylum to a former Peruvian prime minister, prompting Peru's Congress to declare Sheinbaum [[persona non grata]].<ref name="ajz-peru">{{cite news |date=7 November 2025 |title=Peru bans Mexico's President Sheinbaum as diplomatic dispute grows |url=https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/11/7/peru-bans-mexicos-president-sheinbaum-as-diplomatic-dispute-grows |access-date=19 June 2026 |work=[[Al Jazeera]]}}</ref>

Sheinbaum has supported a two-state settlement of the [[Israeli–Palestinian conflict]] and called for recognition of a Palestinian state alongside Israel.<ref name="jpost-palestine2">{{cite news |date=12 October 2024 |title=Mexico's Jewish President Claudia Sheinbaum calls for Palestinian state |url=https://www.jpost.com/international/article-824276 |access-date=19 June 2026 |work=[[The Jerusalem Post]]}}</ref> She condemned the [[Gaza war]] and, in September 2025, described Israel's actions there as a "[[Gaza genocide|genocide]]".<ref name="latimes-genocide2">{{cite web |last=Linthicum |first=Kate |date=22 September 2025 |title=Mexico's Jewish president calls on Israel to end 'genocide in Gaza' |url=https://www.latimes.com/world-nation/story/2025-09-22/mexican-president-claudia-sheinbaum-calls-israeli-assault-on-gaza-a-genocide |access-date=26 September 2025 |website=[[Los Angeles Times]]}}</ref>

=== Approval rating ===
{{Main|Opinion polling on the Sheinbaum presidency}}
Throughout her first year in office, Sheinbaum maintained high public approval ratings, consistently polling above 70%.<ref name=":5">{{Cite web |last=Beauregard |first=Luis Pablo |last2=Flores |first2=Patricia San Juan |date=1 October 2025 |title=Claudia Sheinbaum has higher approval ratings than López Obrador after first year in office |url=https://english.elpais.com/international/2025-10-01/claudia-sheinbaum-has-higher-approval-rating-than-lopez-obrador-after-first-year-in-office.html |access-date=13 December 2025 |website=EL PAÍS English |language=en-us}}</ref><ref name=":7">{{Cite web |date=2 October 2025 |title=President Sheinbaum's first year in office in 12 numbers: Part 2 |url=https://mexiconewsdaily.com/politics/president-sheinbaums-first-year-in-office-in-12-numbers-part-2/ |access-date=24 December 2025 |website=Mexico News Daily |language=en}}</ref> Between January and April 2025, her approval rose to approximately 80%, a surge that several analysts described as a [[rally 'round the flag effect]] following her initial handling of tariffs imposed by U.S. President [[Donald Trump]].<ref name=":7" /><ref>{{Cite web |date=24 February 2025 |title=Aprobación de Sheinbaum sube a 80% por su defensa de México ante Trump, según encuesta |url=https://forbes.com.mx/aprobacion-de-sheinbaum-sube-a-80-por-su-defensa-de-mexico-ante-trump-segun-encuesta/ |access-date=24 December 2025 |website=Forbes México |language=es}}</ref> By December 2025, surveys by ''Enkoll'' and ''[[El Financiero]]'' indicated that her approval had moderated to approximately 70%, coinciding with heightened public concern over violence in states such as Michoacán and broader economic uncertainty.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Moreno |first=Alejandro |date=1 December 2025 |title=Aprobación a Claudia Sheinbaum se mantiene en 70% en noviembre |url=https://www.elfinanciero.com.mx/nacional/2025/12/02/aprobacion-de-claudia-se-mantiene-en-70-en-noviembre/ |access-date=13 December 2025 |website=El Financiero |language=es}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Rios |first=Michael |last2=Torres |first2=Mauricio |date=5 October 2025 |title=From World Cup to a cool head with Trump: why Mexico’s president is still so popular, one year on |url=https://www.cnn.com/2025/10/05/americas/claudia-sheinbaum-popularity-analysis-intl-latam |access-date=13 December 2025 |website=CNN |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Núñez |first=Ernesto |date=5 December 2025 |title=Sheinbaum has high approval ratings, but her government’s troubles are starting to take a toll |url=https://english.elpais.com/international/2025-12-05/sheinbaum-has-high-approval-ratings-but-her-governments-troubles-are-starting-to-take-a-toll.html |access-date=13 December 2025 |website=EL PAÍS English |language=en-us}}</ref> Despite this decline, her disapproval rating remained comparatively low, at about 24%, and her approval continued to exceed that of her predecessor, López Obrador, at the same point in his presidency.<ref name=":5" /><ref name=":6">{{Cite web |last=Harrison |first=Chase |date=1 December 2025 |title=Approval Tracker: Mexico's President Claudia Sheinbaum |url=https://www.as-coa.org/articles/approval-tracker-mexicos-president-claudia-sheinbaum |access-date=13 December 2025 |website=AS/COA |language=en}}</ref>

Demographically, Sheinbaum’s strongest support has been recorded among older adults, with approval ranging from 72% to as high as 86% in late 2025. This demographic is frequently cited as the primary beneficiary of the administration's expanded social programs.<ref name=":6" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Sheinbaum mantiene alta aprobación; llega a primer informe con 70%: encuesta |url=https://www.eluniversal.com.mx/nacion/sheinbaum-mantiene-alta-aprobacion-llega-a-primer-informe-con-70-encuesta/ |access-date=13 December 2025 |website=El Universal |language=es}}</ref> Support has been lower among younger voters, with approval among those aged 18–24 polling between 57% and 66%.<ref name=":6" /><ref>{{Cite web |date=13 November 2025 |title=Marcha del 15 de noviembre: ¿Qué porcentaje de la Generación Z apoya a Sheinbaum? |url=https://www.elfinanciero.com.mx/nacional/2025/11/13/marcha-del-15-de-noviembre-que-porcentaje-de-la-generacion-z-apoya-a-sheinbaum/ |access-date=13 December 2025 |website=El Financiero |language=es}}</ref>

== Political views ==
=== Social issues ===
Sheinbaum is a self-described [[Feminism in Mexico|feminist]], aligning her beliefs and actions with the principles of gender equality and women's rights.<ref>{{Cite web |date=29 September 2020 |title=Soy feminista, pero no apoyo violencia: Sheinbaum |trans-title=I'm a feminist, but I don't support violence: Sheinbaum|url=https://www.capital21.cdmx.gob.mx/noticias/?p=3084 |access-date=7 September 2023 |website=Capital 21 |language=es-MX |archive-date=7 September 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230907180819/https://www.capital21.cdmx.gob.mx/noticias/?p=3084 |url-status=live}}</ref> She advocates for the legalization of [[abortion]], aligning her stance with broader movements aimed at promoting reproductive rights and autonomy for women.<ref>{{Cite news |last1=Rodríguez Mega |first1=Emiliano |last2=Romero |first2=Simon |date=7 September 2023 |title=A Historic First for Mexico as Two Women Vie for the Presidency |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2023/09/06/world/americas/mexico-women-president-candidates.html |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331 |archive-date=8 February 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240208152708/https://www.nytimes.com/2023/09/06/world/americas/mexico-women-president-candidates.html |url-status=live}}</ref> During her leadership in Mexico City, Sheinbaum implemented a gender-neutral policy regarding school uniforms in state-run schools and championed [[LGBT rights]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=4 June 2019 |title=Mexico City unveils gender-neutral school uniforms policy |language=en |work=Reuters |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-mexico-lgbt-uniforms-idUSKCN1T512Q |access-date=7 September 2023 |archive-date=7 September 2023
